正德六年進士登科錄

玉音

正德六年三月初八日，禮部尚書臣費宏等於奉天門奏：「□□會試□□□人，取中三百五十名。本年□□□□□□□殿試，合請讀卷官□□□□□□兼太子太師、吏部尚書、華蓋□□□□□□五十九員，進呈出身等□□□□□□□高皇帝舊制□□□□□□□□□一名，從六品；第二名、三名□□□□□，賜第二甲從七品；第三甲□□□□□□，賜同進士出身。」奏奉聖旨：「是。」欽此。

translation_en:
Record of Metropolitan Graduates of the Sixth Year of Zhengde (1511)

The Imperial Voice

On the eighth day of the third month of the sixth year of Zhengde, your servant Fei Hong, Minister of Rites, and others submitted a memorial at Fengtian Gate: “[Illegible text] the Metropolitan Examination [number of candidates illegible], of whom 350 were selected. For this year’s [illegible text] Palace Examination, we should request the appointment of examination readers [illegible text], concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, Huagai [remainder of title and intervening text illegible], fifty-nine officials in all, to submit the categories of graduate status [illegible text]. Under Emperor Gao’s established regulations [illegible text], the first-place candidate [connection uncertain: ?], lower sixth rank; the second- and third-place candidates [illegible text]; confer upon the second class lower seventh rank [?]; the third class [illegible text], to be granted the status of ‘equivalent to metropolitan graduate.’” In response to the memorial, the imperial command was received: “Approved.” Respect this.

Examination Readers

Li Dongyang was Grand Master for Special Advancement and Glorious Happiness, Left Pillar of State, Junior Preceptor and concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Huagai Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the jiashen year (1464).〕

Yang Tinghe was Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor and concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Jinshen Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year (1478).〕

Liu Zhong was Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Mentor and concurrently Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year (1478).〕

Liang Chu was Grand Master for Glorious Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Guardian and concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall. 〔Metropolitan graduate of the wuxu year (1478).〕

translation_en:
Sequence of Imperial Favors and Honors

On the morning of the fifteenth day of the third month of the sixth year of Zhengde (1511), the tribute scholars proceeded to the inner palace for the Palace Examination. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall and personally bestowed the policy question.

On the morning of the eighteenth day of the third month, [two illegible characters] the civil and military officials attended in their assigned ranks, wearing court dress. That day, the partly illegible text refers to the imperial ceremonial guard arrayed at the vermilion steps and within the vermilion courtyard [?]. The Emperor took his seat in Fengtian Hall. Officials of the Court of State Ceremonial transmitted the imperial decree and called out the names. Officials of the Ministry of Rites carried the yellow list of successful candidates, led by drums and music, out through Chang’an Left Gate and posted it outside. Officials of Shuntian Prefecture then escorted the first-ranked graduate (zhuangyuan) back to his residence with parasols, canopies, and a ceremonial retinue.

On the nineteenth day of the third month…

translation_en:
First Class: three men, granted the distinction of metropolitan graduate with honors (jinshi jidi).

Yang Shen 楊慎 was registered in Xindu County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yongxiu, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was twenty-four years old, born on the sixth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Yang Mei, was a subprefectural clerk, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Preceptor concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory. His grandfather, Yang Chun, was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, posthumously granted the same titles. His father, Yang Tinghe, held those titles. His mother, née Ye, was posthumously granted the title Lady of the First Rank; his stepmother, née Yu, was granted the same title. His grandparents and parents were living. His younger brothers were Dun, a tribute scholar; Zao; Heng, a Secretariat Drafter; Xun; Chen; Quan; and □ [name illegible]. He married a woman née Wang. He placed third in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Ben 余本 was registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang; his household registration category is illegible [□□]. A prefectural school student, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Zihua, and he ranked twentieth among his brothers. His age is illegible [□□]; he was born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Yu Yin, was a prefectural Vice Prefect; his grandfather was Yu Xuan, and his father was Yu Qiande. His mother was née Xia. His father was living and his mother deceased. He married a woman née Xu. He placed eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 191st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou Shouyi 鄒守益 was registered in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a military household. A Confucian scholar, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Qianzhi, and he ranked third among his brothers. He was twenty-one years old, born on the first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zou Shilu; his grandfather, Zou Sijie, was granted the title Left Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review. His father, Zou Xian, was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner. His mother, née Zhou, was granted the title Lady (ruren). His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Shouming and Shoumeng. He married a woman née Wang. He placed sixty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Second Class: 115 men, granted the status of metropolitan graduate (jinshi).

Xu Chengming 許成名 was registered in Liaocheng □, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, in a military household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Siren; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty years old, born on the eighteenth day of an illegible month [?]. His great-grandfather was Si, his grandfather Xin, and his father Mao; his mother was née He and his stepmother née Jia. His father was living. His elder brother was Chengren, and his wife was née Sui. He placed thirty-third in the Provincial Examination of an illegible province and attained an illegible rank in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sheng Yingqi 盛應期 was registered in Shanyin County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang; his household registration category is illegible. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuanlong; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was 𤣱 [reading uncertain], his grandfather Duo, and his father Ze; his mother was née Tian and his stepmother née Yuan. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Liang, □, Ben, Mu, Gai, and Di [names and divisions uncertain]. His wife was née Han. He placed □8th [?] in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Yinglong 馬應龍 was registered in Hezhou, Lintao Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Gongji; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Xiang, and his father Wen; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Quan, Cai, Cong, and Hui. His wife was née Wang. He placed second in the Provincial Examination of an illegible province and forty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zheng Yu 鄭玉, courtesy name Yucheng, was registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-three, born on the fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Qixue, his grandfather Yuanqing, his father Bangli, and his mother née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Zhen and Jing. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Cui. He placed eighth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and thirtieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Mingyang 朱鳴陽, courtesy name Yingzhou, was registered in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, in a civilian household. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first in family order and was aged thirty-two, born on the eleventh day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather Chongtai, his father Wenxing, and his mother née Ye. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Tong, and he married a woman née Xu. He placed thirty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination; his Metropolitan Examination rank is illegible (□□).

Zhang Bi 張璧, courtesy name Chongxiang, was registered in Shishou County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in an official household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third in family order and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-third day of an illegible month (□). His great-grandfather Bishun was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice. His grandfather Ziyan was Assistant Surveillance Commissioner and was additionally granted the posthumous title Grand Master for Governance. His father was Wei, and his mother, née Wang, held the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xi, a tribute scholar; Kui, an Imperial University student; Rui; Yao, an Imperial University student; and Jin. His younger brother is recorded as □bi [?]. He married a woman née Li. He placed twelfth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 108th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ying Liang 應良, courtesy name Yuanzhong, was registered in Xianju County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked seventeenth in family order and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-sixth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Wenzheng, his grandfather Zongru, and his father Changling. His father's former wife was née Xu, his mother was née Xu 許, and his stepmothers were née Sun and née Bao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wen, Shu, He, and Gun, and his younger brother was Shi. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Tu Yingxun 屠應塤 was registered in a military household in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Wenbo and was first in birth order, aged twenty-three, born on the second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Xiang and grandfather Ji were each posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Aid in Governance and Minister of Justice; his father Xun was Minister of Justice, posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent. His legal mothers were née Chen, posthumously titled Lady; née Lin, posthumously titled Lady of Virtue; and née Niu, titled Lady. His birth mother was née Yang. Both parents were recorded as living. His elder brothers were Kui, an Administration Commissioner’s Office Assistant Administration Commissioner, and Yao, an Imperial University student; his paternal cousin Yingjun [?] was a Senior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy. His younger brothers were Bi, Ying□, Yingjun 應埈, Yingdian, Yingfang, Yingshan, and Yingshan [name repeated in the transcription]. He married née Li. He placed thirty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Ming 徐明 was registered in an artisan household in Daxing County, Shuntian Prefecture, and was originally from Changzhou County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Wenzhi and was second in birth order, aged thirty, born on the seventeenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Mengxiong, his grandfather Xian, his father Quan, and his mother née Yu. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Cong; his younger brothers were Rui, Zhong, Gong, Gang, Jian, and Zhong. He married née Liu and subsequently née Fan. He placed sixtieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Chen 吳臣 was registered in a civilian household in Jiyang County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Bolin and was first in birth order, aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Sili, his grandfather Ming, his father Lian, a Prefectural Vice Prefect, and his mother née Zhang. His mother alone was living. His elder brother Wan was a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his younger brothers were Xiang and Ji. He married née Xie. His rank in the Shandong Provincial Examination is illegible (□□); he placed 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Xiang 尹襄 was registered in a civilian household in Yongxin County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Shunbi and was second in birth order, aged twenty-seven, born on the twenty-first day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Mingnan, his grandfather Shiyu, an honorary official recognized for longevity, his father Mo, and his mother née Gao. His mother alone was living. His elder brother Gun was a District Magistrate. He married née Shi. He placed first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and nineteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

黃鍾〔貫直隸隆慶州，民籍，江西贛縣人，州學生，治詩經，字伯魁，行一，年三十六，□月初四日生〕。曾祖澂〔知州〕，祖杲，父寧，前母田氏，母傅氏。慈侍下，弟鏜、銳，娶馮氏。順天府鄉試第六十六名，會試第三百四十九名。

董鋻〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字濟之，行二十二，年三十七，八月初四日生〕。曾祖伯莊，祖文信〔封監察御史〕，父珍〔義官〕，前母倪氏，母王氏。永感下，兄〔鐄、鏵、鑰〔監察御史〕、鍪、鑾、鍊、銃、ヌ〕，弟〔鈿〔陰陽訓術〕、鍂、□、鏻〕，娶丘氏。浙江鄉試第六名，會試第二百六十六名。
translation_en:
Liu Pu 劉朴, courtesy name Huafu, was registered in Changping County, Shuntian Prefecture, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Li, a Judicial Examiner in a Provincial Administration Commission; his grandfather was Tai, a District Magistrate; and his father was Sirong, a Right Administrator. His mother was née Kang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xiang, and his younger brothers were Mo and Zhi. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Chen. He placed eighty-sixth in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and seventy-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Yuan 鄭元, courtesy name Boren, was registered in Yiling Subprefecture, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household, and was originally from Renhe County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty, and born on the sixteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Hezi, his grandfather was Wang, and his father was Wenxiu. His father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Li. He placed eighth in the Provincial Examination; his Metropolitan Examination rank is recorded as 三□□ [?].

Huang Zhong 黃鍾, courtesy name Bokui, was registered in Longqing Subprefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household, and was originally from Gan County, Jiangxi. A subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the fourth day of an illegible month (□). His great-grandfather was Cheng, a Subprefect; his grandfather was Gao; and his father was Ning. His father's former wife was née Tian, and his mother was née Fu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brothers were Tang and Rui. He married a woman née Feng. He placed sixty-sixth in the Shuntian Provincial Examination and 349th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Jian 董鋻, courtesy name Jizhi, was registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was twenty-second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Bozhuang; his grandfather was Wenxin, granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father was Zhen, an honorary official for public benefaction. His father's former wife was née Ni, and his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Huang, Hua, Yue (an Investigating Censor), Mou, Luan, Lian, Chong, and a brother whose name is transcribed as ヌ [?]. His younger brothers were Tian (Instructor in a School of Yin and Yang), Pian [?], a brother whose name is illegible (□), and Lin. He married a woman née Qiu. He placed sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 266th in the Metropolitan Examination.

侯綸〔貫山西太原左衛官籍，直隸滑縣人，府學生，治易經，字廷言，行二，年二十七，六月二十日生〕。曾祖禮〔副千戶〕，祖守賢〔副千戶〕，父盛〔副千戶〕，母張氏〔封宜人〕。慈侍下，兄經〔副千戶〕、統、紋，弟緯、純、紳、約、緒，娶余氏。山西鄉試第三十九名，會試第二百四十八名。

張鵬程〔貫山西平陽府蒲州軍籍，州學生，治易經，字萬里，行一，年二十八，五月二十四日生〕。曾祖迪，祖得林，父翱，母王氏。重慶下，弟鵬翼，娶牛氏。山西鄉試第六十一名，會試第一百五名。

尹重〔貫南京金吾後衛軍籍，直隸江都縣人，國子生，治詩經，字元任，行一，年三十七，八月二十二日生〕。曾祖信，祖敬，父全，母趙氏。永感下，弟約，娶鄧氏，繼娶張氏，聘張氏。應天府鄉試第八十名，會試第二十九名。

陳桓〔貫錦衣衛官籍，福建政和縣人，國子生，治易經，字德威，行五，年二十八，十月二十二日生〕。曾祖寶一，祖君用，父瓊，母劉氏。具慶下，兄郎〔百戶〕、杲、秀〔百戶〕、椿，弟興、調、文、德，娶徐氏，繼娶徐氏。順天府鄉試第四十一名，會試第三百四十名。
translation_en:
Hou Lun, registered in an officer household of the Taiyuan Left Guard in Shanxi and a native of Hua County in Zhili, was a prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tingyan; he ranked second in birth order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the twentieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Li, grandfather Shouxian, and father Sheng were all Vice Battalion Commanders; his mother, née Zhang, had been granted the title Lady of Suitability. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Jing, a Vice Battalion Commander, Tong, and Wen; his younger brothers were Wei, Chun, Shen, Yue, and Xu. He married a woman née Yu. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 248th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Pengcheng, registered in a military household in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, was a subprefectural government student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Wanli; he ranked first in birth order and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-fourth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Di, his grandfather Delin, his father Ao, and his mother née Wang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brother was Pengyi, and he married a woman née Niu. He placed sixty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yin Zhong, registered in a military household of the Jinwu Rear Guard in Nanjing and a native of Jiangdu County in Zhili, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yuanren; he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Jing, his father Quan, and his mother née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Yue. He married a woman née Deng, subsequently married a woman née Zhang, and was betrothed to another woman née Zhang. He placed eightieth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Huan, registered in an officer household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and a native of Zhenghe County, Fujian, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Dewei; he ranked fifth in birth order and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twenty-second day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Baoyi, his grandfather Junyong, his father Qiong, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Lang, a Company Commander, Gao, Xiu, a Company Commander, and Chun; his younger brothers were Xing, Tiao, Wen, and De. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently married another woman née Xu. He placed forty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 340th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Hu Yaoyuan 胡堯元, courtesy name Tingxian, was registered in a civilian household in Puqi County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Youde, his grandfather Hao, and his father Wen, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Shi and his stepmother née Deng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Yaochen, and his younger brothers were Yaokai and Yaomu. He married a woman née Huang. He placed sixty-eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 164th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Cheng 劉城, courtesy name Weihan, was registered in a civilian household in Xincheng County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, and was originally from □ming County, Zhili. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yizhong, his grandfather Bin, his father Xing, and his mother née Mu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Sheng and Ming. He married a woman née Yue. He placed forty-ninth in the Provincial Examination; his Metropolitan Examination rank is missing from the text.

Wang Xuanxi 汪玄錫, courtesy name Tianqi, was registered in a civilian household in Xiuning County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, and was originally from Wuyuan County. An Imperial University student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the sixth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather Duan, and his father Xi, a District Magistrate; his mother was née Hu. Both parents were deceased. He married a woman née Cheng. His rank in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination is illegible (□); he placed fifty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mei 張眛, courtesy name Zhenzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan. A subprefectural government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked sixth among his brothers and was aged twenty-four, born on the fourteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Wenxiu, and his father Boji, an Assistant Instructor; his mother was née Wu and his stepmother née Gong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers are listed as Zhu, Yu, Yin, Ju, Chong (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination year), and Ti [?]. He married a woman née He. He placed fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 329th in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
盛大奇〔貫直隸蘇州府崑山縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字德美，行三，年四十二，十月十九日生〕。曾祖碩，祖宗慶，父晟，母計氏。慈侍下，兄奎、奮，弟奫、太〔同科進士〕，娶曹氏。應天府鄉試第六名，會試第一百七十四名。

王世文〔貫江西吉安府安福縣民籍，國子生，治□□，字質夫，行三，年二十，九月十六日生〕。曾祖莊，祖天麟，父鯨，母萬氏。慈侍下，弟世武、世用、世杰、世俊、世□，娶彭氏。鄉試第六十六名，會試第一百一名。

凌繼文〔貫直隸蘇州府常熟縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字引之，行一，年三十二，十二月二十八日生〕。曾祖師德〔贈刑部主事〕，祖琛〔按察司僉事〕，父麟，母陳氏。重慶下，弟弘文，娶王氏。應天府鄉試第一百十六名，會試第八十八名。

李獻可〔貫直隸河間府景州故城縣軍籍，國子生，治易經，字公從，行一，年三十三，十二月二十九日生〕。曾祖顯清，祖榮〔贈知縣〕，父咨〔監察御史〕，母吳氏〔封孺人〕。永感下，弟際可〔貢士〕、興賢，娶張氏，繼娶戴氏。順天府鄉試第一百二十六名，會試第四十一名。
translation_en:
Sheng Daqi, registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Demei, he was third in birth order, and he was aged forty-two, born on the nineteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuo, his grandfather Zongqing, his father Sheng, and his mother née Ji; his mother alone survived, his elder brothers were Kui and Fen, his younger brothers were Yun and Tai (the latter a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort), and his wife was née Cao; he placed sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 174th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Shiwen, registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in an illegible text (□□); his courtesy name was Zhifu, he was third in birth order, and he was aged twenty, born on the sixteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhuang, his grandfather Tianlin, his father Jing, and his mother née Wan; his mother alone survived, his younger brothers were Shiwu, Shiyong, Shijie, Shijun, and Shi□, and his wife was née Peng; he placed sixty-sixth in the Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ling Jiwen, registered in a military household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yinzhi, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shide (posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice), his grandfather Chen (Assistant Surveillance Commissioner), his father Lin, and his mother née Chen; he had living grandparents and parents, his younger brother was Hongwen, and his wife was née Wang; he placed 116th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xianke, registered in a military household in Gucheng County, Jingzhou Subprefecture, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Gongcong, he was first in birth order, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xianqing, his grandfather Rong (posthumously appointed District Magistrate), his father Zi (Investigating Censor), and his mother née Wu (granted the title Lady, ruren); both parents were deceased, his younger brothers were Jike (a tribute scholar, gongshi) and Xingxian, and he married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Dai; he placed 126th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

吳寅〔貫山西振武衞軍籍，湖廣湘陰縣人，國子生，治書經，字時正，行三，年三十五，十二月初五日生〕。曾祖暄，祖通，父勝，母邢氏。永感下，兄實、憲，弟宸，娶楊氏。山西鄉試第四十五名，會試第三十五名。

許雲鵬〔貫山東東昌府堂邑縣軍籍，國子生，治禮記，字時亨，行一，年二十九，二月二十四日生〕。曾祖全，祖昇〔訓導〕，父廷用〔府通判〕，母陳氏。重慶下，弟雲鳳、雲鸞、雲鶚，娶張氏。山東鄉試第十一名，會試第二十九名。

張孟中〔貫福建福州府閩縣民籍，府學生，治禮記，字道宗，行二，年二十八，八月初三日生〕。曾祖宗孟，祖裡〔贈大理寺寺正〕，父澤〔按察司僉事〕，母林氏〔封孺人〕。慈侍下，兄樂，弟應勅，娶何氏。福建鄉試第四十五名，會試第二百八十一名。

金濂〔貫大寧都司營州中屯衞軍籍，直隸上海縣人，國子生，治書經，字濬之，行五，年三十八，二月二十二日生〕。曾祖廷玉，祖愷〔封刑部郎中〕，父純〔右布政使致仕，進階資德大夫〕，母敬氏〔封宜人〕。具慶下，兄澄〔貢士〕、清，弟漳〔義官〕、澤〔義官〕、淇、潤、滋、瀾，娶門氏，繼娶郭氏。順天府鄉試第二十六名，會試第三百四十八名。
translation_en:
Wu Yin, courtesy name Shizheng, was registered in a military household of Zhenwu Guard, Shanxi, and was a native of Xiangyin County, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuan; his grandfather, Tong; his father, Sheng; and his mother, née Xing. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shi and Xian, and his younger brother was Chen. He married a woman née Yang. He ranked forty-fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and thirty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Yunpeng, courtesy name Shiheng, was registered in a military household of Tangyi County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Quan; his grandfather, Sheng, was an Assistant Instructor; his father, Tingyong, was an Assistant Prefect; and his mother was née Chen. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yunfeng, Yunluan, and Yun'e. He married a woman née Zhang. He ranked eleventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and twenty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Mengzhong, courtesy name Daozong, was registered in a civilian household of Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the third day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongmeng; his grandfather, Li, was posthumously granted the title of Rectifier in the Court of Judicial Review; his father, Ze, was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his mother, née Lin, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Le, and his younger brother was Yingchi. He married a woman née He. He ranked forty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 281st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Lian, courtesy name Junzhi, was registered in a military household of the Yingzhou Central Garrison Guard under the Daning Regional Military Commission, and was a native of Shanghai County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-eight, and born on the twenty-second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tingyu; his grandfather, Kai, was granted the title of Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father, Chun, was a retired Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, advanced to the prestige title of Grand Master for Fostering Virtue; and his mother, née Jing, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability (yiren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Cheng, a tribute scholar (gongshi), and Qing. His younger brothers were Zhang and Ze, both honorary officials for righteousness, followed by Qi, Run, Zi, and Lan. He married a woman née Men and subsequently a woman née Guo. He ranked twenty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 348th in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳應武〔貫直隸揚州府高郵州，民籍，州學生，治書經，字光烈，行四，年三十八，十二月初十日生〕。曾祖讓〔教諭〕，祖子易〔教授〕，父策〔壽官〕，母范氏，繼母湯氏、焦氏。具慶下，兄應疇、應文，弟應奎、應物、應期、應兆，娶韋氏。應天府鄉試第十六名，會試第一百九十七名。

方亮〔貫廣東潮州府揭陽縣，民籍，國子生，治書經，字廷相，行十，年四十，十一日初七日生〕。曾祖瑤，祖孔祥，父孟益，前母宋氏，母陳氏。永感下，兄盛，娶陳氏。廣東鄉試第五名，會試第三百三十六名。

梁億〔貫廣東廣州府順德縣，民籍，直隸太倉州學生，治詩經，字叔永，行六，年四十四，十二月初三日生〕。曾祖楚材〔贈光祿大夫柱國少保兼太子太保吏部尚書武英殿大學士〕，祖直清〔累贈光祿大夫柱國少保兼太子太保吏部尚書武英殿大學士〕，父禮〔順天府儒學訓導，封翰林院編修，累贈光祿大夫柱國少保兼太子太保吏部尚書武英殿大學士〕，母劉氏〔封孺人，累贈一品夫人〕。永感下，兄任〔貢士〕、備〔聽選官〕、儲〔光祿大夫柱國少保兼太子太保吏部尚書武英殿大學士〕、倣、伷〔國子生〕，娶陳氏。廣東鄉試第四十七名，會試第二百十一名。
translation_en:
Chen Yingwu, registered in Gaoyou Subprefecture, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the subprefectural government school. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Guanglie. Fourth in birth order, he was thirty-eight years old and was born on the tenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Rang was a Director of a county school; his grandfather Ziyi was a Professor of a prefectural school; and his father Ce held an honorary office for longevity. His mother was née Fan, and his stepmothers were née Tang and née Jiao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yingchou and Yingwen; his younger brothers were Yingkui, Yingwu 應物, Yingqi, and Yingzhao. His wife was née Wei. He placed sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 197th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Qia, registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county government school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Weihe. Second in birth order, he was thirty-seven years old and was born on the twenty-second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Di, his grandfather Xun, and his father Yun. His father's principal wife was née Pan, and his birth mother was née He. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Yuan, and his wife was née Ding. He placed eighty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 342nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fang Liang, registered in Jieyang County, Chaozhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Tingxiang. Tenth in birth order, he was forty years old and was born on the seventh day, apparently of the eleventh lunar month [?; the transcription reads ‘eleventh day’]. His great-grandfather was Yao, his grandfather Kongxiang, and his father Mengyi. His father's former wife was née Song, and his mother was née Chen. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Sheng, and his wife was née Chen. He placed fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 336th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Yi, registered in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the government school of Taicang Subprefecture in the directly administered metropolitan region. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shuyong. Sixth in birth order, he was forty-four years old and was born on the third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather Chucai was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Master of Glorious Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Guardian concurrently serving as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory. His grandfather Zhiqing received successive posthumous grants culminating in the same titles. His father Li was an Assistant Instructor in the Shuntian Prefecture Confucian school, was honorifically granted the title of Hanlin Academy Compiler, and received successive posthumous grants culminating in Grand Master of Glorious Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Guardian concurrently serving as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory. His mother, née Liu, was granted the title of Lady (ruren) and received successive posthumous grants culminating in Lady of the First Rank. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ren, a tribute scholar; Bei, an official awaiting selection for appointment; Chu, Grand Master of Glorious Happiness, Pillar of State, Junior Guardian concurrently serving as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory; Fang; and Zhou, a student of the Directorate of Education. His wife was née Chen. He placed forty-seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 211th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xu Yingkui, of Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Wenming. He ranked sixty-second in family birth order, was twenty-four sui old, and was born on the twenty-first day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Daosheng, his grandfather Yongquan, his father You, and his mother Lady Rao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yingxuan, Yingji, and Yingbi; his younger brothers were Yingxian and Yinggeng. He married Lady Tan. He placed seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 103rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yuankai, of Zhouzhi County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yaoqing. He ranked second in family birth order, was twenty-six sui old, and was born on the seventh day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Rong was posthumously granted the title of Prefect. His grandfather Xi was a Prefect and was granted the honorary title of Grand Master for Governmental Service (Fengzheng dafu). His father Fu was granted the honorary title of Grand Master for Upright Service (Fengzhi dafu), and his mother, Lady Zhao, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. His mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Yuanzheng, a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) and Department Magistrate, Yuanshan, and Yuanheng. He married Lady Zhang. He placed twenty-third in an examination whose name is partly illegible [?]; the remaining examination information is illegible [?].

Xia Wenhua, of Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Weishun. He ranked eighth in family birth order; his age is illegible [?]. He was born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yingsou was a Prefect, posthumously granted the honorary titles Zhongyi dafu and Zizhi yin. His grandfather was Yi□, his father’s name is illegible [?], and his mother was Lady Jiang. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was Wenying; his younger brothers were Wenshen and another whose name is illegible [?]. He married Lady Bi. He placed thirty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yuanming, of Yifeng County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, was registered in a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Mengfu. He ranked fourth in family birth order, was twenty-four sui old, and was born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chengdao, his grandfather Zhen was an Assistant Instructor, and his father Lun was a District Magistrate. His father’s former wife was Lady Li, and his mother was Lady Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ning, Shi, and one whose name is illegible [?]. He married Lady Liu and subsequently Lady Wang. He placed seventh in an examination whose name is partly illegible [?] and 147th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Bi Jishi, registered in a military household in Guixi County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Rulin, he ranked seventy-second in family birth order, and he was forty-two years old, born on the eighth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Dexing; his grandfather, Yuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education, posthumously appointed a Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his father, Yu, was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner, advanced to the honorary ranks of Chaolie dafu and Xiuzheng shuyin; and his mother, née Jiang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Repose and accorded the title Senior Lady of Suitability. Both parents were deceased; his elder brother, Jichuan, was a Compiler in the Hanlin Academy, his younger brother was Jimin, and his wife was née Qiu; he placed sixty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and three hundredth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Zhong, registered in a military household of Dengzhou Guard, Shandong, and a native of Kunshan County in the directly administered region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuanxiao, he ranked first in family birth order, and he was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-first day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jin, his grandfather was Wenfu, his father was Duo, an honorary official for public benefactions, and his mother was née Zhou; his father was deceased and his mother living, his younger brother's name is illegible (□□), and his wife was née Cao; he placed fifteenth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and one hundred and first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bian Xian, registered in a civilian household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Shizhi, he ranked second in family birth order, and he was forty-three years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi, his grandfather was Wenming, his father was Ji, a Police Chief, and his mother was née Bian; both parents were deceased, his elder brother was Shi, and his wife was née Lu; he placed twelfth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twenty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chai Tai, registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Dehong, he ranked fifth in family birth order, and he was thirty-one years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuo, his grandfather was Zongqing, his father was Sheng, and his mother was née Ji; his father was deceased and his mother living, his elder brothers were Kui, Lian, Qi (a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort), and Yun, and his wife was née Zhang; he placed fourteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and one hundred and thirty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

韓明〔貫浙江紹興府會稽縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字士昭，行二，年三十七，十月十六日生〕。曾祖壽，祖常，父讓〔訓導〕，母勞氏。具慶下，弟聖、聰、銀，娶陳氏。浙江鄉試第二十八名，會試第二百七十二名。

屠滽〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣，民籍，試中書舍人，治詩經，字朝宗，行三，年二十九，十月十八日生〕。曾祖子真〔贈禮部右侍郎〕，祖家生〔贈南京吏部尚書〕，父瑜〔南京吏部尚書〕，嫡母陸氏〔贈夫人〕、姜氏〔封夫人〕，生母方氏。具慶下，兄徑〔義官〕、俓〔光祿寺署丞〕、徲，弟偦〔前軍都督府都事〕、儀〔義官〕，弟佶、俉、仕、僎，娶馬氏。浙江鄉試第五十五名，會試第二百二十七名。

劉翀〔貫江西吉安府永豐縣，民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字士鳳，行七，年二十八，六月十二日生〕。曾祖秉彝，祖叔賛，父昂，母楊氏，繼母毛氏。具慶下，兄頗、穎、頊，弟顧，弟翊、羽、習、翃、翥、翯、翲、翱，娶張氏。江西鄉試第十四名，會試第七名。
translation_en:
Wang Nian 王念, courtesy name Tingsheng, was registered in Qian’an County, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Bin; his grandfather, Zheng, was posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; and his father, He, was Vice Commissioner of a Provincial Surveillance Commission. His father’s former wife, née Gao, was posthumously granted the title Lady (ruren); his mother, née Ma, was granted the same title. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Yu 愈 and Yu 諭, and his wife was née Liu. He placed twenty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 319th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Han Ming 韓明, courtesy name Shizhao, was registered in Kuaiji County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the sixteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Shou; his grandfather, Chang; his father, Rang, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née Lao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Sheng, Cong, and Yin, and his wife was née Chen. He placed twenty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 272nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tu Yong 屠滽, courtesy name Chaozong, was registered in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a civilian household. A probationary Secretariat Drafter specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the eighteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather, Zizhen, was posthumously appointed Right Vice Minister of Rites; his grandfather, Jiasheng, was posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel at Nanjing; and his father, Yu, was Minister of Personnel at Nanjing. His legal mothers were née Lu, posthumously granted the title Lady (furen), and née Jiang, granted the same title; his birth mother was née Fang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Jing 徑, an Honorary Official; Jing 俓, an Assistant Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments; and Ti 徲. His younger brothers were Xu 偦, a Chief Clerk in the Chief Military Commission of the Front Army; Yi 儀, an Honorary Official; and, in a further list of younger brothers, Ji 佶, Wu 俉, Shi 仕, and Zhuan 僎. His wife was née Ma. He placed fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Chong 劉翀, courtesy name Shifeng, was registered in Yongfeng County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked seventh among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the twelfth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Bingyi; his grandfather, Shuzan; his father, Ang; his mother, née Yang; and his stepmother, née Mao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Po 頗, Ying 穎, and Xu 頊; his younger brother was Gu 顧, followed by a further list of younger brothers: Yi 翊, Yu 羽, Xi 習, Hong 翃, Zhu 翥, He 翯, Piao 翲, and Ao 翱. His wife was née Zhang. He placed fourteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Qin Shi, registered in a military household in Jingshan County, Anlu Subprefecture, Huguang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shizhao, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged forty-four, born on the eleventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Tianshou; his grandfather, Zan, was posthumously granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his father, Yongming, was a prefectural Vice Prefect; and his mother, née Yang, was invested with the title Lady of Suitability (yiren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Shuang, and his wife was née Li. He placed sixth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 198th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zou En, registered in an official household of Dezhou Guard in the Directly Administered Region and originally from Wucheng County, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruxi, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jun; his grandfather, Wang, and father, Cheng, were both Company Commanders; and his mother, née Zeng, was invested with the title Lady of Peace (anren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zhong, a Company Commander, and Shu; his younger brothers were Hui and Zhi. His wife was née Song. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 265th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Jifang, registered in a civilian household in Huarong County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, and originally from Jinxian County, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Shiqi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Menghe; his grandfather was Zhao; his father, Rong, was a prefectural Vice Prefect; and his mother was née Liu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Jizhi, Jishan, and Jiwu, and his wife was née Yan. He placed sixty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Peng, registered in a civilian household in Pucheng County, Jianning Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tuannan, he ranked fifth among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-five, born on the eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongan; his grandfather was Mian; his father, Huan, was a Vice Commissioner of a granary; his father's former wife was née Su, and his mother was née Peng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Gui, an honorary official; Huai; Feng, a tribute scholar; and Kun. His younger brother was Xian, and his wife was née Weng. He placed thirtieth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 175th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guan Ji 管楫, courtesy name Ruji, was registered in a military household in Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second in family birth order and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-ninth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yu, his grandfather Ying, and his father Jing; his mother was née Wang. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Xiao, an Instructor in a medical school, Xiang, and Xu; his younger brothers were Zhang and Pu, a Postal Station Master. He married a woman née Li. He placed fiftieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dai Pian 戴楩, courtesy name Weiqian, was registered in a civilian household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A county government school student specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked first in family birth order and was aged twenty-four, born on the seventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Anyi, his grandfather Wenxiang, a Vice Prefect [?], and his father Min, a Prefect; his mother was née Zhang, awarded the title Lady of Suitability, and his stepmother was née Zhan. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brother or brothers are recorded as □□ [illegible]. He married a woman née Sun. He placed 138th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 102nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Dun 汪惇, courtesy name Shuhou, was registered in a civilian household in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education, preceded in the text by an illegible character [?], he specialized in the Record of Rites, ranked eighteenth in family birth order, and was aged forty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Menglin, his grandfather Yansheng, and his father Hu, an Honorary Official; his mother was née Huang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Yi, a County Assistant Magistrate, and Zong, a Granary Vice Commissioner; his younger brothers were Bo, a Daoist Instructor, Kezhang, an Assistant Prefect, Keding, Kexiang, and Kehui. He married a woman née Sun. He placed seventy-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Xian 徐咸, courtesy name Zizheng, was registered in a military household of Haining Guard, Zhejiang, and was a native of Haiyan County. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked fourth in family birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the sixteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shengzong, his grandfather Xiong, and his father Ang; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Fu, Tai, an acting Instructor in a county government school, and Jie; his younger brother was Lin. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 243rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Kuan, of an artisan household registered in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zhongli; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yanxin, his grandfather Yunying, and his father Chong; his mother was née Yang and his stepmother née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhou, Zai, Pu, Zhou, Zhao, and Hai. He married a woman née Jin. He placed forty-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 184th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Fuli, of a military household registered in Dong’an County, Shuntian Prefecture, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zhiren; he ranked eighth among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the eighteenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhong was an Office Director; his grandfather Ying was a County Vice Magistrate, posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of War; and his father Fu was a Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue. His mother, née Wang, was granted the title Lady of Repose. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Fuchu, Guyan, Guxing, and Xuan, and his younger brothers Gushi, Ruzhang, and Ruji. He married a woman née Wang. He placed ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and twentieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Shouli was a native of Puzhou, Shanxi, registered in Xingji County, Hejian Prefecture, and an added-quota student of the Bao’an Subprefectural School specializing in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Bingjie; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the first day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qian; his grandfather Guan was a County Vice Magistrate; and his father Tong was an Assistant Prefect. His legal mother was née Cao and his birth mother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shouren and Shouyi, and his younger brothers Shouzhi, Shouxin, Shoulian, and Shoujie. He married a woman née Yao. He placed fifty-sixth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 293rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Ti, of a military household registered in Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Yaozhang; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shining; his grandfather Ying was posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father Hong was an Administration Vice Commissioner. His mother, née He, was granted the title Lady. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Hu and his younger brother Zhi. He married a woman née Zhai. He placed sixty-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and twenty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Dai En, a civilian registrant of Shanghai County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a prefectural school student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Zichong; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Tingfeng, posthumously appointed Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel; his grandfather was Chun, Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel; his father was Wei, an honorary official for public beneficence; and his mother was née Jiang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was De; his younger brothers were Ci (a tribute scholar), Shu, Zhong, Mao, Yuan, and Yi. His wife was née Hou. He placed seventy-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 218th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Lian, a civilian registrant of Xinyu County, Linjiang Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Chongmei; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhouji, his grandfather Xiangzhen, his father Renliang, and his mother née Qian. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Li, Shan, Pei, and Lin. His wife was née Song. His Provincial Examination rank in Jiangxi was □十六 (an illegible tens digit followed by six); he placed 325th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fei Lin, a civilian registrant of Fengdu County, Zhong Subprefecture, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Derui; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Wenfu, his grandfather Shiying, his father Xiao (a School Instructor), and his mother née Wen. His mother was living and his father deceased. His wife was née Yang; his subsequent wife was née Wen. He placed fifty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 140th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Niu Feng, a civilian registrant of Ye County, Yu Subprefecture, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, was a county school student specializing in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Daozheng; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged forty-two, born on the eleventh day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Gui, his grandfather Lin, his father Duo (a Police Chief), and his mother née Zou. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xuan and Long. His wife was née Ren. He placed seventy-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Mi Fan, registered in a civilian household in Hezhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Tinghui; he ranked third in his family and was aged thirty-seven, born on the eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhi, his grandfather Qing, and his father Xuan; his mother was née Tao and his stepmother née Yao. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Gun, an honorary official, and Yi; his younger brothers were Zan, an honorary official, and Ke. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed fortieth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 121st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fei Cai, registered in a civilian household in Yanshan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zihe; he ranked twenty-sixth in his family and was aged twenty-nine, born on the fourteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rongzu, his grandfather Yingqi, posthumously honored as Grand Master of Government Assistance and Minister of Rites, and his father Yu; his mother was née Zhang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Jun, Hong (Grand Master of Government Assistance and Minister of Rites), Ning, Guan, Wan, and Shi; his younger brothers were Xian and Jin. He married a woman née Lou and subsequently became betrothed to a woman née Wu. He placed forty-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eleventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Dao, registered in a military household in Wucheng County, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Chunfu; he ranked first in his family and was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-ninth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Guangli, his grandfather Lun, and his father Cong; his mother was née Li, and his stepmothers were née Liu and née Yu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Xuan, Yu, Jiong, Mai, and Shi. He married a woman née Li. He placed forty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 126th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Gao, registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Qiming; he ranked sixth in his family and was aged thirty-eight, born on the second day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sen, his grandfather Sitong, and his father Rong; his father's former wife was née Yang and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qing, Zhao, Guan, Xiao, and Lu; his younger brothers were Biao, Hong, Hou, and Li. He married a woman née Wang. He placed twenty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Feng 陸俸 was registered in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, in an artisan household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name is illegible (□□); he was second in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Heqing, his grandfather Yong, and his father □□〔□□〕 (name and annotation illegible); his mother was née Liu and his birth mother née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lun, □, and Wei [?]; his wife was née Xu. He ranked 121st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 318th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Jing 張經 was registered in a military household of the Xingzhou Right Garrison Guard in the directly administered region and was a native of □□ County (name illegible). A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Wenxu; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the sixth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jian, his grandfather Huan, and his father Si; his mother was née Liu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Can, Lun, Zong, Hui, and Bin, and his younger brother was Ji. He married a woman née Wu and subsequently women née Shi and née Wu. He ranked forty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kang De 康德 was registered in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, in a commoner household. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chugui; he was twelfth in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the second day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ziliang, his grandfather Gongche, and his father Bing; his mother was née Fang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Bei, Bao, You, and Si, and his younger brothers were Kan〔a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort〕, Zhi, Ju, and Xin. He married a woman née Dong and subsequently a woman née Chen. He ranked seventy-first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 166th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Yong 盧雍 was registered in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered region, in a commoner household. An additional student of the prefectural Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Shishao; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twelfth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Li, his grandfather Shicheng, and his father Gang; his mother was née Chen and his stepmother née Wu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Xiang. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He ranked 121st in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fifty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Zhan, courtesy name Yingzhong, was from Jintan County, Zhenjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and belonged to a military household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked third in birth order and was aged thirty, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Siwu; his grandfather, Sheng; his father, Yi, a County Magistrate; and his mother, née Rui. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qiao and Gai, and his younger brothers Si and Jun. He married a woman née Gao. He placed eleventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 109th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Ru, courtesy name Pinzhi, was from Gui’an County, Huzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, and belonged to a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked seventh in birth order and was aged thirty-four, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Mian; his father, Hui; and his mother, née Cheng. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Yi, Qiao, Zuo (a Department Magistrate), You, and Dian; his younger brothers were Yan and Pei. He married a woman née Shen. He placed fifty-sixth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and fifty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chao, courtesy name Weixin, was from Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, and belonged to a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he ranked second in birth order and was aged twenty-seven, born on the ninth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Heng; his grandfather, Fuzu [?]; and his father, Daqi, a Records Keeper in the Provincial Administration Commission. His father’s former wife was née Yu, and his mother was née Liu. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers are listed as Tan, Run, Qi, Wei, Jian, Pan, Chong, Hui, Zan, Yi, Hou, Zhi, and Zhi. He married a woman née Ma. He placed eleventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 176th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhu Xu, courtesy name Yaoxu, was from Changzhou County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and belonged to an official household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked first in birth order and was aged thirty-three, born on the third day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Hao, a Right Administration Vice Commissioner in the Provincial Administration Commission; his grandfather, Huan; his father, Yunming, a tribute scholar (gongshi); and his mother, née Li. Both parents and at least one grandparent were living. He married a woman née Shen. He placed 111th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 321st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Jizu, courtesy name Xiaofu, was registered in a civilian household in Yuncheng County, Jining Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Changes. He ranked second [?; the transcription has an extraneous “T”] among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the fourteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather Jing was Left Vice Minister of Justice; his grandfather Qi held a seventh-rank prestige title. His father was Yi, and his mother was née Hou. His mother alone was living. His younger brother was Jizong, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed twenty-ninth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and thirteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Zhen, courtesy name Shiheng, was registered in a civilian household in Kunshan County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An added student of the county Confucian school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xian, his grandfather Qi, and his father Xiao; his mother was née Li. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Wang and Kuo, and his wife was née Gao. He placed eighty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 271st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Can, courtesy name Zhongyu, was registered in an artisan household in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. He ranked second among his brothers and was forty-one years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jinggao; his grandfather Wenxin held the title of honorary official. His father Yun was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Works, and his mother, née Song, was granted the title Lady of Repose. His mother alone was living. His elder brother Wei was a Bureau Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Works; his younger brothers were Qi, Lian, and Zan. His wife was née Zhou. He placed twenty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 188th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Wei, courtesy name Meizhong, was registered in Jiangpu County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a native of Dangtu County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Documents. He ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the nineteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Manwu, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Liang, who held the title of honorary official; his mother was née Song. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xuan and Yu, and his younger brother was Tang. His wife was née Zhao. He placed sixteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Jiacong, courtesy name Weide, was registered in a military household of Zhenwu Guard, Shanxi, and was a native of Xiangyin County, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-five, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Heng; his grandfather, An; his father, Lian, Assistant Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud; and his mother, née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jiaming, Jiahui, Jiazhi, and Jiamo, and his wife was née Yang. He placed fifteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Yizhong, courtesy name Guandao, was registered in a civilian household in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the department school specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Zhen, a County Assistant Magistrate; his father, Chengwen, a student of the Directorate of Education; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jing, Yihe, Yiping, Yipeng, Yiben, Yiyuan, and Yikui [name divisions uncertain: ?], and his wife was née Zhang. His rank in the Shanxi Provincial Examination is illegible (□□□); he placed 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhao Han, courtesy name Hongkui, was registered in a civilian household in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the tenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu; his grandfather, Duan, held an honorary official title for longevity; his father was Bi; and his mother was née Han. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zi, Jia, Jin, and Tao, and his wife was née Lu. He placed forty-eighth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and forty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tong Lun, courtesy name Tingyan, was registered in a military household in Xiaogan County, De’an Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the thirteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhenyi; his grandfather, Xian, a Prefectural Registrar; his father, Rong, held an honorary official title for philanthropy; and his mother was née Cheng. The statement concerning his parents’ survival is illegible (□□) [?]. His elder brother, Jing, was an official awaiting selection for appointment, and his wife was née Xu. He placed fiftieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 292nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Fang 潘倣, courtesy name Jingzhe, was registered in a civilian household in Luoyang County, Henan Prefecture, Henan. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the seventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yunzhong; his grandfather, Zhi; his father, Ji, an Assistant Instructor; and his mother, née Zhang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Xiao, a tribute student; his younger brothers were Ren, Shen, and Yan. He married a woman née Liu. He placed eighty-sixth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 173rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Chang 李長, courtesy name Fuzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Jinyun County, Chuzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked thirty-sixth in his family’s fraternal order and was aged thirty-eight, born on the twenty-first day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xi, posthumously granted the title of Vice Minister of Justice; his grandfather, Qiang; and his father, Hao, a tribute student. His father’s former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Zhu. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Feng, Shi, Mao, and Lü; his younger brother was Xiao. He married a woman née Zheng. He placed forty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 162nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Kang Shichen 康世臣, courtesy name Liangzuo, was registered in a military household of the Shenwu Left Guard and was a native of Bazhou, Shuntian Prefecture. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Classic of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-eight, born on the sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Youyi; his grandfather, Fu, posthumously granted the title of Department Vice Magistrate; and his father, Ding, an Assistant Prefect. His father’s former wives were née Wang, posthumously granted the title of Lady of Peace (anren), and née Xu; his mother was née Wang, granted the title of Lady of Peace. His father alone was living. His elder brother was Jiuxu, an honorary official for public benefactions; his younger brothers were Shilin and Shifeng, the latter entitled to wear official cap and girdle. He married a woman née Feng. He placed 119th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Wensheng 汪文盛, courtesy name Xizhou, was registered in a military household in Chongyang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang. A Confucian scholar specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged twenty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Deheng; his grandfather, Lian, an honorary official for longevity; his father, Zao; and his mother, née Xia. His parents’ survival status is illegible (□□) [?]. His elder brother was Wenming, a county-school Instructor and provincial graduate (juren); his younger brother was Wenzheng. He married a woman née Peng. He placed sixteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 171st in the Metropolitan Examination.
