杜英〔貫順天府寶坻縣民籍，縣學增廣生，治詩經，字子實，行一，年二十五，五月十七日生〕。曾祖□□，祖華，父輗，母陳氏。□□下，弟二中。娶李氏，繼娶張氏。順天府鄉試第一百□名，會試第二百二十五名。
translation_en:
Yu Maojian, registered in a civilian household in Rongchang County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruli, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was twenty-seven years old, born on the thirteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zongrong, his grandfather Zhishan, his father Hong□, and his mother née Yao; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Maoying and Maosheng, and his younger brothers Maogao and Maochong. He married a woman née Hu and subsequently a woman née Wu. He placed seventy-second in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and eighty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sang Yin, registered in a civilian household in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shijiu, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was thirty-two years old, born on the fifteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Qiong, his grandfather Yu, his father Bing, and his mother née Shen; his mother alone was living. His younger brothers were Yi and Dun. He married a woman née Zheng. His ranks in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and the Metropolitan Examination are illegible (□□ in each case).

Liao Mo, registered in a civilian household in Shanghang County, Tingzhou Prefecture, Fujian, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Liangshi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was thirty-one years old, born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather, whose name is illegible (□), was a County Vice Magistrate, posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Rites; his grandfather was Xuan, his father Guangyuan, and his mother née Liang. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Qing, and he married a woman née Liang. He placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 275th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Du Ying, registered in a civilian household in Baodi County, Shuntian Prefecture, was an added student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zishi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was twenty-five years old, born on the seventeenth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather’s name is illegible (□□); his grandfather was Hua, his father Ni, and his mother née Chen. The notation concerning his surviving parents is illegible (□□下) [?]. His younger brother was Erzhong. He married a woman née Li and subsequently a woman née Zhang. His rank in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination is partly illegible (100 + □); he placed 225th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gao Ren, courtesy name Ruyang, was registered in a salt-producing household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Documents; he was first in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongling, his grandfather Tixian, his father Boshao, and his mother née Chen. His parents and a grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Yi, Li, and Zhi, and his wife was née Wu. He ranked forty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 148th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ben, courtesy name Weizhong, was registered in a military household in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Changes; he was third in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twelfth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhi'ang, his grandfather Wenying, his father Yang, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Le and Mu, and his wife was née Kang. His rank in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination is illegible (□□□); he ranked 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Ji, courtesy name Gongji, was registered in a civilian household in Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Documents; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-first day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Rong; his grandfather Zong held an honorary official title conferred for longevity; his father was Duan, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Tan, and his wife was née Zhang. He ranked 110th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jin Gao, courtesy name Heqing, was registered in Mian Subprefecture, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, under a household category transcribed as 人籍 [?], and was a native of Shanghai County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Documents; he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather You was posthumously granted the title of Prefect; his grandfather Jue was Left Administration Vice Commissioner in the Provincial Administration Commission; his father Xianmin was Assistant Surveillance Commissioner in the Provincial Surveillance Commission; and his mother, née Wen, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. His parents and a grandparent were living. His younger brothers were □, □□, □, and Xiao (皛), and his wife was née Wang. His rank in the Sichuan Provincial Examination is illegible (□□); he ranked 142nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Gao Zhi, registered in a military household of Dingliao Central Guard in Liaodong and originally from Jiaozhou, Shandong, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Tingzhen; he was third in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the sixteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Neng; his grandfather, Liang; his father, Sheng, a County Vice Magistrate; and his mother, née Zhao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wenlin and Wenfeng, and his younger brother was Wenpeng. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked thirty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 167th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiang Xin, registered in a military household in Yuechi County, Guang’an Subprefecture, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan, was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Bingcheng; he was fifth in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-third day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Faqing; his grandfather, Quan, posthumously appointed Director of a Bureau in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue; and his father, Shi, a Prefect. His mother, née Lei, was granted the title Lady of Suitability; his stepmother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ren; his elder paternal cousin was Cheng, a retired honorary official; and his younger brothers were Zhen and Yang. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked thirty-seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xiong, registered in an officer household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and originally from Changshan County, Shandong, was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Wenduan; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the twentieth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Youzhi; his grandfather, Xing, a Battalion Commander in the Embroidered-uniform Guard; his father, Gang; and his mother, née Li. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Ying, a Battalion Commander, and his younger brothers were Jun and Jie. He married a woman née Jin and subsequently a woman née Weng. He ranked eighty-sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 200th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Weng Su, registered in a commoner household in Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Chengfu; he was sixth in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the nineteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Rutuan; his grandfather, Hui; his father, Tong; and his mother, née Zheng. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Tong and Xu, and his younger brothers were Ji, Luo, and Qi. He married a woman née Fang. He ranked twenty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 186th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Quanxiao 伍全俲 was registered in a military household in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ruzhen, he ranked seventh among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the twentieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shubin; his grandfather, Yu, held an honorary title for longevity; his father was Tiji, and his mother was née Yan; both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Xiyin and Xirong, his younger brothers were Xizhao, Xizhu, and Xichang, and his wife was née Liu; he placed fourth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 257th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fu Yue 傅鑰 was registered on the banner rolls of Guangning Left Guard in Liaodong and was a student of the guard school specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xizhun, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty, born on the fifth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wang, his grandfather was Xiang, and his father was Jing; his legal mother was née Tang and his birth mother was née Zhang; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Zhao and Zhen, and his wife was née Song; he placed sixty-seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 208th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Yin 宋寅 was registered in a civilian household in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Weiqing, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongzhen, his grandfather was Wanfang, his father was Gongyong, and his mother was née Luo; his father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brothers were Huan and Kuan, and his wife was née Chen; he placed fifty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 185th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ouyang Song 歐陽嵩 was registered in a civilian household in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Ruzhong, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Tang, was a Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather, Xian, was a Prefectural School Instructor; his father was Tingchen, and his mother was née Xiao; both parents were living; his elder brother was Xiang, his younger brothers were Gui and Kun (the latter a metropolitan graduate in the same examination cohort), and his wife was née Xiao; he placed ninetieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and sixteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Yiqi, courtesy name Shizhao, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was originally from Wu County in the directly administered metropolitan region. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-fourth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Min; his grandfather, Guan, was an honorary official; his father was Lun; his mother was née Ji, and his stepmother née Liu. Both parents were living. His wife was née Liu. He ranked eighty-fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 192nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Can, courtesy name Jingchuan, was registered in a military household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. A county school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-five, and born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Bingren; his grandfather, Shanzhao, was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; his father, Gang, was an honorary official; and his mother was née Liang. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Huai, Xu [?], Han, Bian, Song, Pei, Yong, Pang, Hao, Xun, and Qian. His wife was née Tan. He ranked forty-third in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and sixty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qu Yue, courtesy name Bingjun, was registered in a military household in Pucheng County, Huazhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the fourth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhi; his grandfather was Shen; his father, Ning, had been granted the title of Judge; and his mother, née Sun, had been granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brother, Quan, was an Assistant Prefect; his younger brothers were Cheng and Rui. His wife was née Jia. He ranked thirtieth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 118th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pan Han, courtesy name Chaozong, was registered in a military household in Tiantai County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-seven, and born on the sixteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shangde; his grandfather was Mingmei; his father was Yonghua; and his mother was née Sun. His mother was living, and his father was deceased. His elder brother was Wang; his younger brother was Zhou, followed in the transcription by the garbled text “bf” [?]. His wife was née Lu. He ranked fifty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 227th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liu Hong 劉浤 was from Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, registered in a Confucian scholar household, and a student of the Directorate of Education; he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals, had the courtesy name Chimei, ranked eleventh in family order, and was aged forty-one, born on the eighteenth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Hu, his grandfather Jun, and his father Ji, a prestige official of the seventh rank; his mother was née Zhou, and both parents were living. His elder brothers were 𥘼 [reading uncertain] and Xiang, a prefect; his younger brothers were Qiu, Xi, Fu, Shang, and Ge. His wife was née Wang. He placed fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dou Ming 竇明 was from Wuxiang County, Qinzhou, Shanxi, registered in a commoner household, and a student of the Directorate of Education; he specialized in the Book of Documents, had the courtesy name Weiyuan, ranked first in family order, and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Zhen, and his father Ziwen, a patrol inspector; his father's former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Ma. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brothers were Yun, Guang, Xiong, and Biao; his younger brother was Hu. His wife was née Wu, and his subsequent wife was née Ren. He placed sixty-eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 316th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Hui 吳惠 was from Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, registered in a commoner household, and a student of the Directorate of Education; he specialized in the Book of Changes, had the courtesy name Renfu, ranked third in family order, and was aged thirty-two, born on the fifth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Ziliang, his grandfather Zhen, his father Shan, and his mother née Zhu; both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Kui, and his younger brother Jin. His wife was née Xu. He placed eleventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and tenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Mao 孫懋 was from Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, registered in a commoner household, and a student of the Directorate of Education; he specialized in the Book of Poetry, had the courtesy name Defu, ranked thirteenth in family order, and was aged forty-three, born on the ninth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Lei, a secretary in the Ministry of Works; his grandfather was Song, his father Wenyuan, a district magistrate, and his mother née Chen. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His younger brother was Zhi. His wife was née Liu, and his subsequent wife was née Chen. He placed eighty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 317th in the Metropolitan Examination.

龔□入〔貫四川順慶府南充縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字循矩，行一，年三十二，九月二十六日生〕。曾祖銘，祖璟，父洪，母樊氏。重慶下，弟賢霖、顯、孟元，娶楊氏。四川鄉試第三十九名，會試第二百九十九名。

徐文溥〔貫浙江衢州府開化縣民籍，縣學生，治春秋，字可大，行三，年三十二，八月十八日生〕。曾祖用括〔醫官〕，祖綿〔義官〕，父琦，母詹氏。慈侍下，兄文洪〔監生〕，弟文瀚、文濟、淓、浤、潤、津、文涇，娶許氏。□□鄉試第十一名，會試第一日二十三名。

賈啟〔貫留守中衛官籍，湖廣黃岡縣人，順天府學生，治詩經，字啟之，行七，年三十一，元月初七日生〕。曾祖鉉〔指揮僉事〕，祖浩〔指揮同知〕，父汝楫〔府通判〕，母毛氏。永感下，兄鈍〔指揮僉事〕、愚、魯、蒙、柔、太，娶丘氏。順天府鄉試第六名，會試第八十五名。

黃大源〔貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，府學增廣生，治詩經，字與潔，行一，年四十二，九月二十三日生〕。曾祖惟耕，祖學廣〔贈知縣〕，父燮〔知縣〕，母丘氏。□□下，弟文清、文瀚、文洙、文洗、文浴、文淬、文濡，娶林氏。□□鄉試第五十九名，會試第二百六十三名。
translation_en:
Gong □ru 龔□入 [?] was registered in a military household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Imperial University, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Xunju; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather Jing, his father Hong, and his mother Lady Fan. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Xianlin, Xian, and Mengyuan [name divisions uncertain]. He married Lady Yang. He placed thirty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 299th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Wenpu 徐文溥 was registered in a civilian household in Kaihua County, Quzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang. A county school student, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. His courtesy name was Keda; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-two years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yongkuo, a medical official; his grandfather was Mian, an honorary official; his father was Qi, and his mother Lady Zhan. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother Wenhong was an Imperial University student; his younger brothers were Wenhan, Wenji, Fang, Hong, Run, Jin, and Wenjing. He married Lady Xu 許. He placed eleventh in the Provincial Examination of an illegible locality (□□) and 123rd [?; the transcription reads 第一日二十三] in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jia Qi 賈啟 was registered in an officer household of the Central Guard of the Rear Garrison and was a native of Huanggang County, Huguang. A student of the Shuntian prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Qizhi; he ranked seventh among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, an Assistant Commander; his grandfather was Hao, an Associate Commander; his father was Ruji, an Assistant Prefect; and his mother was Lady Mao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Dun, an Assistant Commander, and Yu, Lu, Meng, Rou, and Tai. He married Lady Qiu. He placed sixth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Huang Dayuan 黃大源 was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian. An additional student of the prefectural school, he specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yujie; he ranked first among his brothers and was forty-two years old, born on the twenty-third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Weigeng; his grandfather was Xueguang, posthumously granted the title of District Magistrate; his father was Xie, a District Magistrate; and his mother was Lady Qiu. The notation concerning his parents’ survival is illegible (□□). His younger brothers were Wenqing, Wenhan, Wenzhu, Wenxi, Wenyu, Wencui, and Wenru. He married Lady Lin. He placed fifty-ninth in the Provincial Examination of an illegible locality (□□) and 263rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

簡霄〔貫廣西柳州府馬平縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字汝欽，行一，年二十九，四月二十一日生〕。曾祖寬，祖琮〔壽官〕，父文〔布政司經歷〕，母郝氏。永感下，弟弼〔貢士〕，娶鄭氏。廣西鄉試第二名，會試第七十三名。

史立誠〔貫浙江寧波府鄞縣民籍，國子生，治易經，字克明，行五，年三十七，七月初二日生〕。曾祖必初，祖仕珉，父本欽，母何氏，繼母王氏。具慶下，弟立讓、立誌、立詳、立謙、立議、立諶、立訓、立詔、立諭，娶范氏。浙江鄉試第百十四名，會試第二百六名。

桂萼〔貫江西饒州府安仁縣民籍，縣學生，治詩經，字子實，行九，年三十四，六月二十四日生〕。曾祖珍〔旌表義民〕，祖俊，父暲，母倪氏。慈侍下，兄華，娶吳氏。江西鄉試第十九名，會試第三百二十六名。

陳霑〔貫直隸真定府冀州民籍，州學生，治詩經，字汝霖，行三，年三十二，六月初七日生〕。曾祖剛，祖瑛，父謨〔府知事〕，前母胡氏，母池氏。慈侍下，兄貫、貢、需，娶張氏，繼娶韓氏。順天府鄉試第三十四名，會試第一百五十三名。
translation_en:
Jian Xiao, registered in a military household in Maping County, Liuzhou Prefecture, Guangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Ruqin; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-nine, born on the twenty-first day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Kuan; his grandfather, Cong, held an honorary longevity title; his father, Wen, was Office Manager in a Provincial Administration Commission; and his mother was née Hao. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother Bi was a tribute scholar (gongshi). His wife was née Zheng. He placed second in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi Licheng, registered in a civilian household in Yin County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Keming; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was thirty-seven, born on the second day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Bichu, his grandfather Shimin, and his father Benqin; his mother was née He and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Lirang, Lizhi, Lixiang, Liqian, Liyi, Lichen, Lixun, Lizhao, and Liyu. His wife was née Fan. He placed 114th in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 206th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gui E, registered in a civilian household in Anren County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zishi; he ranked ninth among his brothers and was thirty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Zhen had received official commendation as a righteous commoner; his grandfather was Jun, his father Zhang, and his mother née Ni. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Hua, and his wife was née Wu. He placed nineteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 326th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Zhan, registered in a civilian household in Jizhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a department government school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Rulin; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-two, born on the seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Gang; his grandfather, Ying; and his father, Mo, a prefectural Clerk. His father's former wife was née Hu, and his mother was née Chi. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers are listed as Guan, Gong, and Xu [?]. His wife was née Zhang; he subsequently married a woman née Han. He placed thirty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Chen Mei, registered in Fushun County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Defu; he ranked second in birth order and was twenty-eight, born on the eleventh day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Yizheng, his grandfather Benzhao, and his father Zhong; his mother was née Huang. His father was deceased and his mother living. He married a woman née Liu. He placed thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 229th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Shiyuan, registered in Zhaozhou, Zhending Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bosheng; he ranked first in birth order and was thirty, born on the eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Fusheng; his grandfather Shun was posthumously appointed Case Reviewer; and his father Min was Right Administration Vice Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission. His mother, née Mao, was granted the title Lady (Ruren), and his stepmother was née Chen. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Shiheng, a student admitted by virtue of his father's office, and Shili. He married a woman née Liu. He placed 114th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 315th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Wan, registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Minxing; he ranked eighth in birth order and was twenty-seven, born on the ninth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhenyi, his grandfather Ping, and his father Liang. His father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Shi and Zhe. He married a woman née Yun. He placed fourth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 163rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yingqi, registered in Renhe County, Hangzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yuanji; he ranked third in birth order and was twenty-five, born on the sixteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Ao; his grandfather Peng held honorary official status for charitable contributions; and his father Hui was a Medical Instructor. His father's principal wife was née Shen, his stepmother née Pan, and his birth mother née Chen. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Yingyou, Yingxiang, Yingti, Yingzuo, Yinglun, and Yingrao. He married a woman née Mo. He placed thirty-fourth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 311th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
□□□ (name illegible), courtesy name Bainian, was from Ba County, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan, registered in a military household, and a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Rites; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Mao, his grandfather Yan□□ [?], his father Qianzhong, and his mother née Wei; his mother was living and his father deceased, his younger brothers were Cheng, Ji, and Tai, and his wife was née Cao. He placed fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 240th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Dechong, courtesy name Daofu, was from Wenshang County, Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, registered in a civilian household, and a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-eight years old, born on the fourth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Li, his grandfather Lin 〔a Post Station Master〕, his father Ben 〔a retired Administrator〕, and his mother née Guo; his father was apparently living and his mother deceased [?], his younger brother was Dexin, and his wife was née Zhao. His first examination ranking is damaged, with only the final “eight” legible [?]; he placed 189th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xianfang, courtesy name Mengchun, was from Dai Subprefecture, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, registered in a civilian household, and a student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the sixteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Fuyuan, his father Zi 〔illegible annotation〕, his mother née Zhi, and his stepmother née Wang; both parents were living, his younger brothers were Xianhua, Xianfan, Xianrong, Xianmao, and Xianyu, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed eighty-eighth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 122nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cao Lan, courtesy name Defang, was from Xianning County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, registered in a military household, and an Instructor at the county school of Changyuan, in the directly administered metropolitan region; he specialized in the Book of Documents, ranked second among his brothers, and was thirty-six years old, born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month. The great-grandfather entry is damaged [?]; his grandfather was Fu, his father Gong, and his mother née Zhao; the statement of his parents’ survival is illegible [?], his younger brothers were Zhi, Qin, and Ling, and his wife was née Wang. He placed sixth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ba □□ [?] was registered in the civilian register of Zhaozhou, Dali Prefecture, Yunnan, and was a native of Dali Guard. He was a student of the Imperial University; the text concerning his specialization in the Book of Documents is partly illegible [?]. His courtesy name was Wenjian. Fifth in birth order, he was thirty-five years old and was born on the eighteenth day of the intercalary second month. His great-grandfather was Cheng, his grandfather Jing, and his father Xiu〔entered official service [?]〕; his mother was née Cheng. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Hua, Zun, Bi, Ding, Kai, and Tai, and his younger brothers Sheng, Nian, Su, Zhe, and Yue. He married a woman née Chen. He placed ninth in the Yunnan Provincial Examination and twenty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Kui was registered in the military register of Xiangyuan County, Luzhou, Shanxi, and was a county school student. He specialized in the Book of Rites, and his courtesy name was Shunbi. Second in birth order, he was twenty-four years old and was born on the twenty-third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Duan〔posthumously appointed Investigating Censor〕; his grandfather was Jie〔Right Vice Minister of War, concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, posthumously awarded the prestige titles Grand Master for Deliberation and Assistant in Governance [?]〕; his father was Fengyi〔Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice〕; and his mother was née Zhang〔enfeoffed as Lady〕. The statement concerning his parents’ survival is illegible [?]. His elder brother was Long〔Compiler in the Hanlin Academy〕, and his younger brothers were Yuan, Kai, and Yi. He married a woman née Qin. His Provincial Examination jurisdiction and part of his rank are illegible: he placed □ tens [?]. He placed 195th in the Metropolitan Examination.

□□□ [name illegible] was registered as a military artisan in Wugong Central Guard and was a native of Wujiang County in the directly administered metropolitan territory. He was an added-quota student of the Shuntian Prefectural School. He specialized in the Book of Documents, and his courtesy name was Xinchen. First in birth order, he was twenty-four years old and was born on the eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Cheng〔posthumously appointed Bureau Secretary in the Ministry of Works〕; his grandfather was Zeng〔honorary official in recognition of longevity〕; his father was Zi; and his mother was née Cheng. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Jie, and he married a woman née Shen. He placed sixty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Guangda was registered in the civilian register of Cixi County, Ningbo Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was an added-quota student of the county school. He specialized in the Book of Odes, and his courtesy name was Tixing. Second in birth order, he was thirty-eight years old and was born on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather’s name is illegible; his grandfather was Yanyou, his father Zhen〔an official of a River Anchorage Office〕, and his mother née Yu. The statement concerning his parents’ survival is illegible [?]. His elder brothers were Guangji〔tribute scholar〕 and Guangyuan. He married a woman née Tang. He placed seventy-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 124th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
…registered in Yifeng County, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan, in a military household, and a student of the Directorate of Education. □□Fan 藩 specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yiping. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-seven and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yan 巖, an unranked official; his grandfather was Qing 慶, granted the title of Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue and posthumously awarded that of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; his father was Tinggui 廷珪, an Assistant Prefect; and his mother, née Jia, was granted the title of Lady of Suitability. His mother was living and his father deceased. His younger brothers were Weiyuan and Weiping. He married a woman née Hu. He ranked sixteenth in the Provincial Examination and 161st in the Metropolitan Examination.

□□Kui 奎 was registered in Yidu County, Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong, in a civilian household, and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Wenhuan. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-five and was born on the second day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Xuan 瑄, an honorary longevity official; his grandfather was □; his father was Luan 鸞; and his mother was née Zhao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Yingbi and Yingqi. He married a woman née Qiao. He ranked seventy-sixth in the Provincial Examination and 144th in the Metropolitan Examination.

□□□ was registered in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, in a household of illegible registration category, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Defu. Third in birth order, he was aged twenty-six and was born on the fourteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was □; his grandfather was Zeshan; and his father was Kui 夔, a Department Magistrate. His legal mother was née Yin, and his birth mother was née Qiu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Jian 瑊 and Qing 卿, and his younger brothers were Huan 瓛 and Lu 璐. He married a woman née Tian and subsequently a woman née Zeng. He ranked fifty-fourth in the Provincial Examination and 350th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jie 王傑 was registered in Jingyang County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, in a civilian household, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Wenying. First in birth order, he was aged thirty-four and was born on the sixteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Jingchun; his grandfather was Zonghong; his father was Liangyu; and his mother was née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. He married a woman née Cheng. He ranked fourteenth in the Provincial Examination and 345th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
You Lian 游璉 was registered in a civilian household in Lianjiang County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Shizhong and ranked fifth among his brothers; he was thirty-six years old, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yisheng, his grandfather Li, his father Yu, and his mother née Zhao. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Jia, Xuan, and Zhu, and his younger brothers Cong and Guan. He married a woman née Yang. He ranked sixty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tian Jing 田荆 was registered in a military household in Lanzhou, Lintao Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was a native of Li County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Pingyou and ranked second among his brothers; he was twenty-eight years old, born on the thirtieth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongning, his grandfather Yi, and his father Tang; his father's principal wife was née Gao, and his birth mother was née Liu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Wan, and his younger brothers Qin and Zao. He married a woman née Yang. He ranked forty-eighth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Aizhi 李愛之 was registered in a civilian household in Jiading Subprefecture, Sichuan. A subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Jiajing and ranked first among his brothers; he was thirty-three years old, born on the eighth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shichang, his grandfather Benzong, his father Guan (Magistrate), and his mother née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brother was Chengzhi. He married a woman née Wu. He ranked twenty-eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 302nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Chong 張翀 was registered in a civilian household in Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Xizhi and ranked fourth among his brothers; he was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-first day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhong, his grandfather Wenxiu, and his father Boji (Assistant Instructor); his mother was née Wu and his stepmother née Gong. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Zuo and Xu, and his younger brothers Jian and Qu (a metropolitan graduate of the same examination cohort). He married a woman née Du. He ranked eighth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and forty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

李校〔貫江西吉安府安福縣軍籍，國子生，治春秋，字彥甫，行二，年三十八，三月初十日生〕。曾祖志節，祖崇弁，父讓，母彭氏。永感下，兄標、柯〔義官〕、梡，弟材、橋、柟、梃、櫏，娶賀氏。江西鄉試第四十二名，會試第一百五十六名。
translation_en:
Nie Gong 聶珙 was registered in a civilian household in Shanggao County, Ruizhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Guoxian. He ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the first day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yiduan; his grandfather, Yan, was an Unranked Functionary; his father was Ji, and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qiong and Zhang. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently a woman née Mao. He placed sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 289th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Luan 余鑾 was registered in a military household in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A prefectural government school student, he specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Tingyi. He ranked third among his brothers, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the twenty-second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Congdao, his grandfather Xin, his father Zhigao, and his mother née Fang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were 𨯔 [reading uncertain] and Yu 鈺, and his younger brother was Mou. He married a woman née Yao. He placed sixty-sixth in the Huguang [Provincial Examination?; two characters illegible] and 224th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Mu 鄭慕 was registered in a salt-producing household in Fuqing County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian. A county government school student, he specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shishun. He ranked ninth among his brothers, was aged forty-three, and was born on the tenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Du, his grandfather Kui 㙓, and his father Lu, a District Magistrate. His father's principal wife was née Zeng, and his birth mother was née Wang. His parents were deceased. His elder brother Tian was an Assistant Instructor. He married a woman née Han. He placed forty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 297th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Xiao 李校 was registered in a military household in Anfu County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education, he specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Yanfu. He ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the tenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhijie, his grandfather Chongbian, his father Rang, and his mother née Peng. His parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Biao, Ke, an honorary official, and Kuan; his younger brothers were Cai, Qiao, Nan, Ting, and Qian. He married a woman née He. He placed forty-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 156th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Dai Zhu, registered in Taiping County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military household and was an expanded-quota student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yunhua, he ranked sixth in birth order, and he was twenty-four years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the intercalary first month. His great-grandfather was Wenheng, his grandfather Shikuan, his father Shangben, and his mother née Hu; both parents were living; his elder brothers were Ji, Yin, Qian, Tai, and □ [illegible]; he was betrothed to a woman née Zhao; he placed seventy-seventh in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 237th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Bingzhong, registered in Wugong County, Qian Subprefecture, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Minzhi, he ranked first in birth order, and he was forty years old, born on the tenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was An, his grandfather Jian, his father Zhou, an Assistant Instructor, and his mother née Zhang; both parents were living; his younger brother was Yunzhong; he married a woman née Qiao; he placed fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 270th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Ji, registered in Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Zigong, he ranked fourth in birth order, and he was forty-one years old, born on the twenty-fourth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Hong, an honorary official recognized for longevity, his grandfather Liang, his father Zan, his father’s former wife née Kong, and his mother née Zhong; both parents were deceased; his elder brothers were Yun, Lin, and Ting, the last an annual tribute student; he married a woman née Xia and subsequently a woman née Chen; he placed fifty-eighth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 107th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Xiangfeng, registered in Hongtong County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Guozhen, he ranked second in birth order, and he was thirty-eight years old, born on the twenty-first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shitai, his grandfather Ban, his father Xuan, Commissioner of a Transport Office, his father’s former wife née Li, and his mother née Zhang; his father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Jiugao and his younger brother Mingfeng; he married a woman née Hao; he placed seventeenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 301st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yan Shitai, registered in a civilian household in Jiangxia County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, and originally from Yuyao County, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Yingjie, he ranked seventh among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-two, born on the twelfth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shou'an, his grandfather Jie, his father Yi (an honorary official), and his mother Lady Shi; both parents were living; his elder brothers were Shizhan (an official awaiting selection for appointment), Shixian (a tribute scholar, gongshi), and Shiyong, and his younger brother was Shiying; he married Lady Xu and placed thirty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 182nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Heng, registered in a medical household in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yuanzhen, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-eight, born on the eighteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lu (posthumously awarded the title “Dazheng Tongzheng” [?]), his grandfather Zongwu (Left Vice Minister of Rites), his father Fu, and his mother Lady Cai; his father was deceased and his mother living; his younger brother was Jing (an honorary official); he married Lady Jiang and placed □□ in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Rong, registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Qingzhou Left Guard school in Shandong specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Junxi, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the twenty-fourth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Debao, his grandfather Yinbin, his father Yonghe, and his mother Lady Shi; his father was deceased and his mother living; he married Lady Yao and placed forty-fourth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 127th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Tao Lin, registered in an artisan household in Wu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Renfu, he ranked first among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-nine, born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yongchang, his grandfather Yu, his father Ji, and his mother Lady Tang; both parents were deceased; he married Lady Cai and placed forty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 205th in the Metropolitan Examination.

李潤〔貫濟州衛軍籍，山西蒲州人，國子生，治易經，字子雨，行二，年三十五，八月十二日生〕。曾祖忠，祖信，父賢，母楊氏。慈侍下，兄海，弟滄，娶何氏。順天府鄉試第三十九名，會試第七十四名。

徐乾〔貫廣西桂林府臨桂縣民籍，府學生，治易經，字健夫，行一，年二十八，九月二十二日生〕。曾祖亨，祖麟〔義官〕，父斆〔知縣〕，母劉氏，繼母朱氏。重慶下，弟覲、升、拫、有，娶費氏。廣西鄉試第三名，會試第二百三十四名。

胡鳳〔貫浙江金華府湯溪縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字時鳴，行四，年三十三，十二月初五日生〕。曾祖宗傑，祖彥信，父孟琁，母趙氏。慈侍下，兄僖、儉、儲，娶吳氏。浙江鄉試第八十三名，會試第二百五十一名。

謝珊〔貫湖廣荆州府松滋縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字白聲，行一，年二十二，正月十八日生〕。曾祖輓〔知府同〕，祖槩〔□作〕，父茂〔監生〕，母陶氏，繼母陳氏。嚴侍下，弟玖、瑚、珠、璡、瓉，娶胡氏。湖廣鄉試第三名，會試第一百三十六名。
translation_en:
Li Run, courtesy name Ziyu, was registered in a military household of Jizhou Guard and was a native of Puzhou, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twelfth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather, Xin; his father, Xian; and his mother, née Yang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Hai, and his younger brother, Cang. He married a woman née He. He placed thirty-ninth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Qian, courtesy name Jianfu, was registered in a civilian household of Lingui County, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-eight, and born on the twenty-second day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Heng; his grandfather, Lin, an Honorary Official; his father, Xiao, a District Magistrate; his mother, née Liu; and his stepmother, née Zhu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Jin, Sheng, Hen, and You. He married a woman née Fei. He placed third in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and two hundred thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hu Feng, courtesy name Shiming, was registered in a civilian household of Tangxi County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the fifth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zongjie; his grandfather, Yanxin; his father, Mengxuan; and his mother, née Zhao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xi, Jian, and Chu. He married a woman née Wu. He placed eighty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and two hundred fifty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Shan, courtesy name Baisheng, was registered in a civilian household of Songzi County, Jingzhou Prefecture, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-two, and born on the eighteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Wan, a Prefect [?; the annotation reads 知府同]; his grandfather, Gai, whose annotation is unclear (□作) [?]; his father, Mao, an Imperial University student; his mother, née Tao; and his stepmother, née Chen. His father was living and his mother deceased. His younger brothers were Jiu, Hu, Zhu, Jin, and Zan. He married a woman née Hu. He placed third in the Huguang Provincial Examination and one hundred thirty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

傅楫，貫福建泉州府南安縣，軍籍，國子生。治易經，字廷濟，行三，年二十八，八月十八日生。曾祖振〔贈戶部主事〕，祖凱〔戶部郎中〕，父浚〔工部員外郎〕，母莊氏〔封安人〕。重慶下，兄桓、棟，弟材、柟、楷，娶趙氏。福建鄉試第七十五名，會試第九十八名。

鄭正義，貫直隸池州府建德縣，民籍，國子生。治詩經，字宜之，行一，年二十八，十月二十二日生。曾祖方，祖亶，父文明，嫡母沈氏，生母馮氏。具慶下，弟正行、正中、正和，娶柯氏。應天府鄉試第五十九名，會試第二百六十八名。

徐蘭，貫江西建昌府廣昌縣，民籍，國子生。治詩經，字天秀，行九，年三十五，七月十六日生。曾祖泰寧，祖資直〔贈刑部主事〕，父昭，母余氏。具慶下，兄𨱋〔倉副使〕，弟蕐、葛〔貢士〕、道、茂，娶揭氏。江西鄉試第三十五名，會試第二百三十九名。

董相，貫河南河南府嵩縣，民籍，縣學生。治易經，字應期，行三，年二十六，八月二十七日生。曾祖環，祖士哻，父□，母蔣氏。□□下，娶王氏。河南鄉試第七十三名，會試第二百五十九名。
translation_en:
Fu Ji, registered in Nan’an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Tingji, and he ranked third among his brothers. He was twenty-eight and was born on the eighteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was Kai, a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his father was Jun, a Vice Director in the Ministry of Works; and his mother, née Zhuang, held the title Lady of Peace. His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Huan and Dong, and his younger brothers were Cai, Nan, and Kai. His wife was née Zhao. He placed seventy-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and ninety-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Zhengyi, registered in Jiande County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Yizhi, and he ranked first among his brothers. He was twenty-eight and was born on the twenty-second day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fang, his grandfather was Dan, and his father was Wenming. His legal mother was née Shen, and his birth mother was née Feng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhengxing, Zhengzhong, and Zhenghe. His wife was née Ke. He placed fifty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 268th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Lan, registered in Guangchang County, Jianchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Tianxiu, and he ranked ninth among his brothers. He was thirty-five and was born on the sixteenth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Taining; his grandfather was Zizhi, posthumously granted the title of Secretary in the Ministry of Justice; his father was Zhao; and his mother was née Yu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Ling (𨱋) [?], a Vice Commissioner of a Granary; his younger brothers were Hua, Ge (a tribute scholar), Dao, and Mao. His wife was née Jie. He placed thirty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 239th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dong Xiang, registered in Song County, Henan Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the county Confucian school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yingqi, and he ranked third among his brothers. He was twenty-six and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Huan, his grandfather was Shihan [?], his father’s name is illegible (□), and his mother was née Jiang. The statement concerning his parents’ survival is illegible (□□下) [?]. His wife was née Wang. He placed seventy-third in the Henan Provincial Examination and 259th in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉廷簠〔貫富峪衛軍，江西貴溪縣人，國子生，治春秋，字器重，行三，年四十，四月初十日生〕。曾祖士敏，祖希佐〔義官〕，父震彖，母習氏，繼母彭氏。永感下，兄廷策、廷籌，弟廷築，娶朱氏。順天府鄉試第一百十五名，會試第八十二名。

李鳳〔貫山東萊州府平度州昌邑縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字仲鳴，行五，年三十三，十月二十五日生〕。曾祖復仁，祖志剛，父昇，前母王氏，母張氏。永感下，兄熊、豹、鸞、鷹，弟鴻，娶潘氏，繼娶宋氏。山東鄉試第八名，會試第五十六名。

沈俊〔貫直隸廬州衛官籍，泰州人，府學生，治書經，字人傑，行一，年三十九，五月十一日生〕。曾祖德聲，祖瑛〔指揮同知〕，父紀〔聰選官〕，母楊氏。具慶下，娶劉氏。應天府鄉試第一百十九名，會試第二百十七名。
translation_en:
Ren Shunchen 任舜臣, courtesy name Chenghua, was registered in a military household in Sanyuan County, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged thirty-four, and born on the ninth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yong, his grandfather Jing, his father Xiang, and his mother née Duan; his mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Yaochen, and his younger brothers were Xichen, Yuchen, Wenchen, Wuchen, and Zhouchen. He married a woman née Shen. He ranked ninth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 187th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Tingfu 劉廷簠, courtesy name Qizhong, was registered with the military of Fuyu Guard and was a native of Guixi County, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, he was third in birth order, aged forty, and born on the tenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shimin, his grandfather Xizuo (an honorary official for charitable service), his father Zhentuan, his mother née Xi, and his stepmother née Peng. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tingce and Tingchou, and his younger brother was Tingzhu. He married a woman née Zhu. He ranked 115th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Feng 李鳳, courtesy name Zhongming, was registered in a civilian household in Changyi County, Pingdu Subprefecture, Laizhou Prefecture, Shandong. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-fifth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Furen, his grandfather Zhigang, and his father Sheng; his father’s former wife was née Wang, and his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xiong, Bao, Luan, and Ying, and his younger brother was Hong. He married a woman née Pan and subsequently a woman née Song. He ranked eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and fifty-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Jun 沈俊, courtesy name Renjie, was registered in an officer household of Luzhou Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a native of Taizhou. A prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-nine, and born on the eleventh day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Desheng, his grandfather Ying (Vice Commander), his father Ji (an official described as 聰選官 [?]), and his mother née Yang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Liu. He ranked 119th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 217th in the Metropolitan Examination.

劉佐〔貫陝西延安府中部縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字以道，行一，年二十九，正月初六日生〕。曾祖準，祖景〔贈知府〕，父聰〔前資政大夫、都察院右僉都御史〕，母張氏〔封恭人〕。重慶□，弟儼〔監生〕、侃、倌、仁，娶屘氏。陝西鄉試第十一名，會試第二百七十三名。

王鑾〔貫南京錦衣衛籍，直隸吳江縣人，國子生，治易經，字汝和，行二，年四十三，六月初三日生〕。曾祖文昭，祖信，父潤，母闞氏，繼母楊氏、吳氏。具慶下，兄欽，弟釜、鐸、錦，娶尹氏。應天府鄉試第三十九名，會試第九十四名。

裴繼芳〔貫山西平陽府霍州靈石縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字世賢，行二，年四十八，十二月二十六日生〕。曾祖思孝，祖珪，父泰〔知州〕，前母梁氏，母任氏。慈侍下，兄紹芳〔知縣〕，弟繩芳，娶趙氏。山西鄉試第五十一名，會試第六十八名。
translation_en:
Xia Shangpu 夏尚朴 was registered in a civilian household in Yongfeng County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he had the courtesy name Dunfu and ranked thirty-sixth in family order. He was forty-six years old, born on the third day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Mengcheng, his grandfather Yuangui, his father Guanghong, and his mother née Ye. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother Shang’an was a Sacrificial Assistant; his younger brother was Shangzhi. He married a woman née Liu. He placed twenty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 326th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Zuo 劉佐 was registered in a military household in Zhongbu County, Yan’an Prefecture, Shaanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Yidao and ranked first in family order. He was twenty-nine years old, born on the sixth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhun; his grandfather Jing was posthumously appointed Prefect. His father Cong formerly held the prestige title Grand Master for Assisting in Governance and served as Right Assistant Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His mother, née Zhang, was invested with the title Lady of Respect. Parents and grandparents were living [?; the final character of the formula is illegible]. His younger brothers were Yan, an Imperial University student, Kan, Guan, and Ren. He married a woman née Man [?; transcribed as 屘]. He placed eleventh in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 273rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Luan 王鑾 was registered with the Nanjing Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Wujiang County in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Ruhe and ranked second in family order. He was forty-three years old, born on the third day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenzhao, his grandfather Xin, and his father Run. His mother was née Kan; his stepmothers were née Yang and née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Qin, and his younger brothers were Fu, Duo, and Jin. He married a woman née Yin. He placed thirty-ninth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninety-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Pei Jifang 裴繼芳 was registered in a civilian household in Lingshi County, Huo Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Shixian and ranked second in family order. He was forty-eight years old, born on the twenty-sixth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sixiao, his grandfather Gui, and his father Tai, a Subprefect. His father’s former wife was née Liang, and his mother was née Ren. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother Shaofang was a Magistrate; his younger brother was Shengfang. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed fifty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and sixty-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

punctuated:
林有孚，貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，府學生。治書經，字以吉，行十，年三十一，九月初八日生。曾祖宏泰〔贈通議大夫都察院右副都御史〕，祖良弼〔禮科給事中贈通議大夫都察院右副都御史〕，父元甫〔通議大夫都察院右副都御史〕，母陳氏〔贈淑人〕，継母孔氏〔封淑人〕。慈侍下，兄有年〔知縣〕、有恒〔監生〕、有祿〔同知〕、有早〔義官〕、有教，弟有容，娶黃氏。福建鄉試第六名，會試第六十四名。

姚爵，貫陝西平涼府靜寧州軍籍，國子生。治春秋，字汝修，行一，年三十二，九月十五日生。曾祖福，祖文義，父瑾〔都司經歷〕，母劉氏。慈侍下，兄唐〔監生〕、錫，弟壽，娶石氏。陝西鄉試第五名，會試第八十一名。

宋廷佐，貫□西□□府乾州武功縣□，國子生。治詩經，字良弼，行二，年三十五，六月初六日生。曾祖端〔贈通議大夫南京大理寺卿〕，祖寧〔贈通議大夫南京大理寺卿〕，父欽〔南京大理寺卿進階資政大夫正治上卿致仕〕，前母侯氏〔贈淑人〕，母由氏〔封淑人〕。慈侍下，兄廷輔，娶王氏。順天府鄉試第四十三名，會試第六十三名。

郭清，貫福建興化府莆田縣軍籍，國子生。治詩經，字直夫，行二，年三十四，七月十二日生。曾祖師凱，祖宗訓，父伯玉，母吳氏。具慶下，兄湍〔教諭〕，娶吳氏。福建鄉試第十名，會試第一百十四名。
translation_en:
Lin Youfu was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and was a prefectural government student. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yiji. He ranked tenth in his family, was aged thirty-one, and was born on the eighth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather Hongtai was posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His grandfather Liangbi was a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Rites, posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate. His father Yuanfu held those same two titles. His mother, née Chen, was posthumously granted the title Lady (shuren); his stepmother, née Kong, was granted the same title. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Younian, a County Magistrate; Youheng, an Imperial University student; Youlu, an Associate Prefect; Youzao, an Honorary Official for Righteousness; and Youjiao. His younger brother was Yourong. He married a woman née Huang. He placed sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Jue was registered in a military household in Jingning Subprefecture, Pingliang Prefecture, Shaanxi, and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Ruxiu. He ranked first in his family, was aged thirty-two, and was born on the fifteenth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Fu, his grandfather Wenyi, and his father Jin, a Registrar in a Regional Military Commission. His mother was née Liu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Tang, an Imperial University student, and Xi; his younger brother was Shou. He married a woman née Shi. He placed fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Tingzuo was registered in Wugong County, Qian Subprefecture, in an illegible prefecture in a province transcribed as “□xi” [?]; the following registration designation is also illegible. He was an Imperial University student and specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Liangbi. He ranked second in his family, was aged thirty-five, and was born on the sixth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Duan and grandfather Ning were each posthumously granted the titles Grand Master for Thorough Counsel and Minister of the Court of Judicial Review at Nanjing. His father Qin was Minister of the Court of Judicial Review at Nanjing, advanced to the rank of Grand Master for Aid in Governance and the honorary title Senior Minister of Orthodox Governance, and had retired. His father's former wife, née Hou, was posthumously granted the title Lady (shuren); his mother, née You, was granted the same title. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Tingfu. He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Qing was registered in a military household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and was an Imperial University student. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zhifu. He ranked second in his family, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the twelfth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Shikai, his grandfather Zongxun, and his father Boyu; his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brother Tuan was a Director of a county Confucian school. He married a woman née Wu. He placed tenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and one hundred fourteenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

姜清〔貫江西廣信府弋陽縣民籍，國子生，治書經，字源甫，行十七，年二十九，八月初八日生〕。曾祖度〔訓導〕，祖璧，父綰〔按察使〕，母周氏。慈侍下，兄承恩，弟溥、深、淅、泓，娶李氏。江西鄉試第十七名，會試第二百二十二名。

沈健〔貫福建興化府莆田縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字若乾，行一，年三十三，六月二十六日生〕。曾祖永璘，祖居安，父資德，母黃氏。具慶下，弟佑，娶林氏。福建鄉試第□□名，會試第二百一十二名。

梁穀〔貫山東兗州府東平州民籍，國子生，治易經，字仲用，行五，年二十九，八月十九日生〕。曾祖繼祖〔贈戶部郎中〕，祖安〔知府，贈監察御史〕，父覲〔按察司副使〕，前母李氏，母孔氏。慈侍下，兄□、稔〔鴻臚寺署丞〕、槩〔義官〕、丕，娶孔氏。山東鄉試第七名，會試第二百六十九名。
translation_en:
Jiang Qing 姜清, registered in a civilian household in Yiyang County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Yuanfu, he ranked seventeenth among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the eighth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Du, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Bi; his father was Wan, a Surveillance Commissioner; and his mother was née Zhou. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brother was Cheng'en, and his younger brothers were Pu, Shen, Xi, and Hong. His wife was née Li. He placed seventeenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 222nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Jian 沈健, registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Ruoqian, he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-sixth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yonglin; his grandfather was Ju'an; his father was Zide; and his mother was née Huang. Both parents were living; his younger brother was You, and his wife was née Lin. His rank in the Fujian Provincial Examination is illegible (□□); he placed 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bi Tinggong 畢廷拱, registered in a military household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Jingfu, he ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged forty-three, born on the tenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Boren; his grandfather was Rixiong; his father was Yu; and his mother was née Wu. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were Yuan, an Instructor, and Tingcan, and his younger brothers were Tinghan and Tingjian. His wife was née Deng. He placed twenty-second in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 244th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liang Gu 梁穀, registered in a civilian household in Dongping Subprefecture, Yanzhou Prefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhongyong, he ranked fifth among his brothers and male cousins, and he was aged twenty-nine, born on the nineteenth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jizu, posthumously granted the title of Director in the Ministry of Revenue; his grandfather was An, a Prefect, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; and his father was Jin, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Kong. His father was deceased and his mother living; his elder brothers were □ [name illegible], Ren, an Assistant Office Director in the Court of State Ceremonial, Gai, an honorary official, and Pi. His wife was née Kong. He placed seventh in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 269th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Yuyan, courtesy name Jikuan, was registered in Meizhou, Sichuan, in a civilian household and was an added-quota student at the county school of Zhouzhi, Shaanxi. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry, ranked first among his brothers, and was forty-seven years old, born on the eighteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Siliang; his grandfather, Wenguang; his father, Puzhong, an official awaiting selection for appointment; and his mother, née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Yuhe and Yujing. He married a woman née Huang and subsequently another woman née Huang. He placed seventh in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and twelfth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jie, courtesy name Shouzhi, was registered in an official household of the Nanjing Front Guard of the Rear Military Commission and was a native of Jurong County, Yingtian Prefecture. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Classic of Changes. He apparently ranked second among his brothers and was forty years old [the rank-and-age wording is garbled: 十四十]; he was born on the twelfth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zhen, and grandfather, Jing, were both full chiliarchs; his father, Xiong, held an honorary official designation (enrong guan) [?]. His father's former wife was née Lu, and his mother was née Fu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Fu, a chiliarch, Zuo, and Jian. He married a woman née Liu. He placed twenty-seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Si, courtesy name Yixue, was registered in Taihe County, Ji'an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a military household. He was a student of the Directorate of Education, specialized in the Classic of Poetry, ranked fourth among his brothers, and was thirty years old, born on the twenty-ninth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather, Zhi, was Junior Preceptor [?; transcribed 少傳], concurrently Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and Minister of Personnel, and was posthumously awarded the title Grand Guardian and the name Wenduan. His grandfather, Ji, received the honorary title Secretariat Drafter and subsequently the posthumous title Registrar of the Chief Military Commission. His father, Qiu, was a prefectural judge. His father's former wife, née Yang, was posthumously awarded the title Lady of Suitability; his mother, née Ren, received the same title during her lifetime. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Nian, Qing, Gong, and Yu; his younger brother was Chou. He married a woman née Hu. He placed seventy-second in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and fifty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Guo Jiugao, courtesy name Mingshi, was registered in an artisan household of the Yiyong Front Guard and was a native of Jiangdu County in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education, specialized in the Classic of Changes, ranked first among his brothers, and was twenty-seven years old, born on the twenty-second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan; his grandfather, Rong; his father, You, a prestige official of the seventh rank; and his mother, née Meng. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Jiucheng and Jiuwan. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed twenty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Li Ji 李楫, courtesy name Daji, was registered in an officer household of Chengdu Central Guard, Sichuan, and was a native of Yiwu County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-nine, and was born on the eleventh day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhiguang was a Battalion Commander; his grandfather Qian was a Vice Battalion Commander; and his father Shi was an Assistant Administrator in a Provincial Administration Commission. His father's principal wife, née Wang, was granted the title Lady of Suitability (yiren); his birth mother was née Quan. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother Ji was a Vice Battalion Commander; his younger brothers were Pu, Kai, Huan, and Zhu. He married a woman née Yang and subsequently a woman née He. He placed forty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 285th in the Metropolitan Examination.

He Bi 何璧, courtesy name Wenzheng, was registered in a military household of Taicang Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a native of Huangyan County, Zhejiang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the twenty-ninth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sidao, his grandfather Gui, and his father Qi. His father's former wife was née Han, and his mother was née Zheng. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother was Kui. He married a woman née Hua and subsequently a woman née Qiu. [Six illegible characters: □□□□□□] eighty-seventh place; the examination is unidentified [?].

Yin Jing 尹京, courtesy name Zhaozhi, was registered in a military household of Dahe Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region and was a native of Anfu County, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked fourth among his brothers, was aged forty-two, and was born on the twentieth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ergong; his grandfather Zheng was honorifically appointed a Secretary in the Ministry of Works; and his father Zhen was a Prefect. His mother, née Xiang, was granted the title Lady of Peace (anren). Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wen, Zhang, and Gao; his younger brothers were Qi, Xuan, Li, and Bao. He married a woman née Ma and subsequently women née Chen and née Zhu. He placed eighty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 223rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Cheng'en 孫承恩, courtesy name Zhenfu, was registered in a civilian household of Huating County, Songjiang Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he ranked second among his brothers, was aged thirty, and was born on the thirteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shida; his grandfather Huan was an Assistant Instructor, posthumously appointed a Bureau Director; and his father Yan was a Prefect. His father's principal wife, née Yao, and his stepmother, née Wang, were each granted the title Lady of Suitability (yiren); his birth mother was née Ruan. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Yong, Mu, and Chengde. He married a woman née Wu. He placed seventy-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and eighty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Liao Qing 廖慶, courtesy name Tishan, was a county school student registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, and specialized in the Book of Odes. Fifth in birth order, he was aged thirty and born on the second day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shengzong, his grandfather Wengui, and his father Daxun; his mother was née Chen. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His wife was née You. He ranked eighty-sixth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 131st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xu Zhiluan 徐之鸞, courtesy name Ruiqing, was an Imperial University student registered in a military artisan household in Tongcheng County, Anqing Prefecture, Zhili, and specialized in the Book of Odes. First in birth order, he was aged twenty-nine and born on the eighth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Chen; his grandfather Xiang was posthumously granted the title of Registry Manager of Yingtian Prefecture. His father was Ying, and his mother was née Jin. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Zhifeng and Zhilong, and his wife was née Yuan. He ranked thirty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventeenth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Fen 王蕡, courtesy name Shizhen, was an Imperial University student registered in a civilian household in Jinxi County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, and specialized in the Book of Changes. Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-eight and born on the twenty-second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Zhong was a Police Chief, posthumously granted the title of Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review; his grandfather was Ji. His father Xu was an Instructor, granted the title of Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice; his mother, née Zeng, was granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brother Xuan was a Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Justice, and his younger brother was Qin. His wife was née Fu. He ranked twenty-seventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and twenty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Ji 伍箕, courtesy name Chaohui, was an added-quota student in the county school, registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and specialized in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Tenth in birth order, he was aged thirty-five and born on the twenty-eighth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather Mian was a District Magistrate, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his grandfather Tixiang was granted the title of Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice. His father was Xiyu; his father’s former wife was née Xie, and his mother was née Wang. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Fu, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner, Fan, Zuan, and Lu; his younger brothers were Jian, Ce, Bian, and Fei. His wife was née Peng. He ranked seventy-ninth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and seventy-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.
