translation_en:
He Jin 賀縉 was registered in Yongxin County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a civilian household, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chaoqing; he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-four, born on the twenty-fourth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Henghuo; his grandfather, Wen, was a county magistrate; his father was Yi, and his mother was née Xiao. His mother alone survived. His elder brothers were Shao and Hui; his younger brothers were Chuo, Jing, Xuan, Hong, Chun, and Hui. His wife was née Shi. He placed ninety-first in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 320th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gao Peng 高鵬 was registered in Lizhou, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, in a medical household, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Yunyi; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the fifteenth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xin; his grandfather, Lian, was a government student; his father was Tang, and his mother was née Ding. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were E and He. His wife was née Zhou. He placed sixty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination; his Metropolitan Examination rank is recorded as □□七, with two illegible characters before “seven.”

Zhang Xuan 張璿 was registered in Yuyao County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, in an official household, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Shunyong; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the fifteenth day of the second lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ji; his grandfather was Hao; his father was Wei, and his mother was née Ye. His mother alone survived. His younger brothers were Yu, Shan, Rui, Qi, and Yi. His wife was née Han. He placed twenty-second in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 334th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Bidong 汪必東 was registered in Chongyang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, in a military household, and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Xihui; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the fifteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhimei; his grandfather was Ming; his father was Zhenlong, and his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Bihao, Bideng, and Biyang; his younger brothers were Bixing, Biheng, and Bilian. He married a woman née Ai and subsequently a woman née Zhou. He placed thirty-second in the Provincial Examination for a jurisdiction whose name is illegible (□□), and fifty-fifth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Shan, registered in Guichi County, Chizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Desheng, he was third in birth order, and he was aged thirty, born on the eleventh day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Lansen, his grandfather Zhen, his father Song, and his mother née Wu; both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ying and Can (a student of the Directorate of Education), and his younger brothers were Hu, Cui, Ji, Xiang, Qi, and Jie; his wife was née Wang. He placed twenty-third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 252nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Nan Daji, registered in Weinan County, Huazhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a military household and was an additional student of the county Confucian school specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Yuanshan, he was first in birth order, and he was aged twenty-five, born on the third day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yan, his grandfather Gui, his father Jin (an Assistant Instructor), and his mother née Jiao; both parents were living. His younger brother was Fengji, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed fourth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 119th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yan Shitai, registered in an official household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and originally from Putian County, Fujian, was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shouhong, he was fifth in birth order, and he was aged forty-four, born on the twenty-second day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Jianing (posthumously appointed Investigating Censor), his grandfather Jin (an Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy, posthumously appointed Minister of Revenue), and his father Bin (Grand Master for Fostering Goodness, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent). His father’s former wife was née Zhang (posthumously granted the title Lady), his mother was née Lai (granted the title Lady), and his stepmother was née Huang (granted the title Lady); both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Sa (a student of the Directorate of Education), Hu and Yun (both honorary officials for public benefactions), Xiang, and Si (an Assistant Office Director in the Court of Imperial Entertainments); his younger brothers were Ji, Shu, Yong, and Lian, and his wife was née Chen. He placed fortieth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and sixty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Jiang Gan, registered in Quanzhou, Guilin Prefecture, Guangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Rujie, he was sixth in birth order, and he was aged twenty-five, born on the eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Shibao, his grandfather Hong, and his father Quan (a District Magistrate); his father’s former wife was née Tang, and his mother was née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Guan, Zi, Ying, Lan, and Huai, and his younger brothers were Shu, Han, Hu, Fu, and Ming; his wife was née Tang. He placed fourth in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and 343rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wu Gao 吴杲, registered in a civilian household in Yixing County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Mengyin; he ranked second among his brothers and was forty-five years old, born on the eighteenth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Di; his grandfather, Ke, was posthumously appointed Secretary in the Ministry of War; his father, Zhen, was Secretary in the Ministry of War; and his mother, née Wu, was granted the title Lady of Peace (anren). His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother was Dan and his younger brother Bing. He married a woman née Fan, and subsequently women née Jiang and née Wu. He placed eighty-fifth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 132nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Quan 劉泉, registered in a civilian household in Anfu County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, was an supplementary student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Yingzhan; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-one years old, born on the eighth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yuxiu; his grandfather, Wei, was granted the title Left Assistant Judge in the Court of Judicial Review; his father, Chao, was Left Assistant Administration Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; and his mother, née Gao, was granted the title Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. An illegible family detail ends with the character Yong 永 [?]. He married a woman née Zhou. His Provincial Examination location and rank are illegible; his Metropolitan Examination rank is partly illegible, ending in “thirteen” [?].

Lin Jun 林俊, registered in a civilian household in Putian County, Xinghua Prefecture, Fujian, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruying; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-five years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of an illegible month. His great-grandfather was Zi, his grandfather Yu, his father Tingyu, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Zhu. He placed first in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen Qi 沈圻, registered in a salt-producing household in Pinghu County, Jiaxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zijing; he ranked third among his brothers and was twenty-two years old, born on the ninth day of the second month. His great-grandfather, Wei, was granted the title Secretary; his grandfather, You, was posthumously appointed Secretary; his father, Lian, was Right Assistant Administration Commissioner in a Provincial Administration Commission; and his mother, née Bao, was granted the title Lady of Peace (anren). His parents and grandparents were living. His elder brothers were Kai and Yin; his younger brothers were Jiang, Kun, Tai, Tian, Jiong 坰, Po, Pi, Gai, Hao, Jiong 埛, and Pao. He married a woman née Lu. He placed eighteenth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Sheng Jiao, courtesy name Zongxia, was registered in a civilian household in Yancheng County, Xuzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A county government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers; his age is damaged in the text (□□五) [?], and he was born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather Ji was a Transport Commissioner, posthumously granted the title Grand Master of Palace; his grandfather Kai was an Instructor in the School of Yin and Yang. Four characters, apparently concerning his father, are illegible [?]; his mother was née Hu. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Shi, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed thirty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination and 295th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Sun Shaozu, courtesy name Yuanzong, was registered in a military household of Zhenwu Guard, Shanxi, and was a native of Daizhou. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-six years old, born on the twenty-seventh day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Cai; his grandfather was Sheng; and his father, Zhang, was a tribute scholar, posthumously appointed Examining Editor in the Hanlin Academy. His mother, née Zhang, was granted the title Lady. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brother Shaoxian was a metropolitan graduate and Investigating Censor; his younger brothers were Shaokuan, Shaozou, Shaotao, Shaozhong, Shaolie, and Shao□. His wife was née Liu. He placed sixteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 194th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Jingyu, courtesy name Canzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Nanxi County, Xuzhou Prefecture, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked tenth among his brothers and was twenty-five years old, born on the first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Wan; his grandfather, whose name is illegible, was a Prefectural School Instructor, posthumously appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue. His father, Xin, was a metropolitan graduate and Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue. His mother, née Ming, was granted the title Lady of Peace. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Jingchun, Jing□, Jingyi, Jingxuan, a tribute scholar, and Jingyin, a County Magistrate; his younger brother was Jingzong. His first wife's surname is illegible; his subsequent wife was née Ou. He placed thirty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 101st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Chengde, courtesy name Runzhi, was registered in a civilian household in Puzhou, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A subprefectural government school student specializing in the Book of Changes, he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-four years old, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Bojing; his grandfather was Xin; and his father, whose name is illegible, was a Director of Food Service. His mother was née Wen, and his stepmother was née Zhang. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xi, Kuang, Rui, Gang, Yue, Chuan, Quan, Shengxian, an Imperial University student, Shengzhang, also an Imperial University student, and Zhen; his younger brothers were Qi and Tan. His wife was née Fan. He placed twenty-eighth in both the Shanxi Provincial Examination and the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Third class: 231 graduates, granted the status of graduates equivalent to metropolitan graduates (jinshi).

Zhao Guan was registered in a civilian household in Hezhou, Chongqing Prefecture, Sichuan. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Weixian and was sixth in family order, aged thirty, born on the twenty-sixth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Yiren; his grandfather, Zhong, was a District Magistrate; and his father, Yingju, was an Assistant Prefect. His father's former wife was née Li, and his mother was née Qin. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Ning, a District Vice Magistrate; Kuan, an honorary official recognized for righteousness; Jun; and Yi. His wife was née Song. He placed eleventh in the Sichuan [□□] Examination [?] and 112th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xun Feng was registered in a military household of the Tingzhou Guard, Fujian. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he had the courtesy name Ruiqing and was first in family order, aged thirty, born on the twentieth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather, Wentong, held an honorary title for longevity; his grandfather was Zhi; his father was Yongmao; and his mother was née Xu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Fengxiang and Fengshao, and his wife was née Zhang. He placed seventy-ninth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 339th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shigao was registered in a civilian household in She County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he had the courtesy name Jingzhou and was fifteenth in family order, aged twenty-eight, born on the fourteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Jizu; his grandfather was Hongguan; his father was Siyou; and his mother was née Cheng. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Quan, Zhen, and Yue; his younger brothers were Lian, Tang, Xi, and Zun. His wife was née Jiang. He placed sixty-second in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 254th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Jin Li, courtesy name Shiyue, was registered in Linqing Subprefecture, Dongchang Prefecture, Shandong, under a school registration [?]. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Puyuan; his grandfather, Cong; his father, Xi, a Commissioner; and his mother, née Li. Both parents were living. His younger brother was Hong, and he married a woman née Xu. He placed sixty-eighth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 264th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Xinglu, courtesy name Jinzhi, was registered in an official household in Liyang County, Yingtian Prefecture. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was third in birth order; his age is partly illegible (□□十三) [?], and he was born on the twenty-first day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xinke; his grandfather, Gongfu, posthumously granted the title Gentleman for Service; his father's name is illegible, and his father served as a Registrar in an illegible office [?]; his mother, née Wang, was granted the title Lady. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xing□ and Xingshan, and he married a woman née Xu. The examination record reads “Yingtian Prefecture [illegible] examination, fifth place” [?].

Wang Xi, courtesy name Zhizhi, was registered in a military household in Yishi County, Pu Subprefecture, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Songs, he was first in birth order, aged forty-seven, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Haowen; his grandfather, Gui; his father, Da; his mother, née Xie; and his stepmother, née Wei. His parents and grandparental generation were living. His younger brother was Qin. He married a woman née Han and subsequently a woman née Huang. He placed fourteenth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 242nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yao Wenqing, courtesy name Lianfu, was registered in a civilian household in Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi. An additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-two, and born on the twenty-first day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Lin, posthumously granted the office of Prefectural Vice Prefect; his grandfather, Yu, was Right Administrative Assistant in a Provincial Administration Commission; his father, Lun, was a tribute scholar (gongshi). His father's former wife was née Lu, and his mother was née Zheng. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Wenpei, Wenpu, and Wenhao; his younger brother was Wenzao. He married a woman née Chu. He placed sixty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 324th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ye Yong, registered in Taiping County, Taizhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a military salt-producing household and was an additional student at the county school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Shiguan. First in birth order, he was twenty-eight years old and was born on the second day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Shizhou, his grandfather Shangwen, and his father Yunzai; his mother was née Sun and his stepmother née Zhou. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ying and E, and his wife was née Yu. He ranked first in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and thirty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Song Yue, registered under a military banner in the Wugong Central Guard and originally from Wuding Subprefecture, Shandong, was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Dewei. Second in birth order, he was thirty-four years old and was born on the twenty-second day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zhongfu; his grandfather Fu was Vice Commissioner of the Institute of Fine Crafts under the Ministry of Works; his father Cheng was Vice Commissioner of the Mint Office under the Ministry of Works. His mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother Jian was a tribute scholar; his younger brothers were Chong, Jian (a company commander in the Wugong Central Guard), Zhong, Kai, and □ [name illegible]. His wife was née Xu. He ranked eleventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Jiang, registered in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Imperial University. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Zongmin. Third in birth order, he was thirty-three years old and was born on the fourteenth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhongde, his grandfather Yuan, and his father Zhao; his father's former wife was née Ju and his mother née Li. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brothers were Ji and Han, his younger brother was Jie, and his wife was née Li. He ranked first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and forty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Wenming, registered in Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, belonged to a military household and was a student at the prefectural school. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Yingkui. Third in birth order, he was twenty-three years old and was born on the fifth day of the third month. His great-grandfather was Xue, his grandfather Weiqian, and his father Lu; his mother was née Li and his stepmother née Nie. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Wenlin and Wengao, his younger brother was Wenyu, and his wife was née Luo. He ranked twenty-fourth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 177th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
He Yue, courtesy name Xunbo, was registered in a civilian household in Jiangning County, Yingtian Prefecture, and was a native of Wujiang County in the directly administered region. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fourth in birth order; his age is illegible [?]. He was born on the second day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Wenguang; his grandfather Cheng and father Xuan both held honorary offices for longevity. His mother was née Li. His father alone was still living. His elder brothers were Zhong, Jian (a student of astronomy), and Duo, and his younger brother was Qin. He married a woman née Wang. He placed fifteenth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 215th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Fan Lu, courtesy name Yizai, was registered in a military household in Guiyang County, Chenzhou, Huguang. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked eleventh in birth order and was thirty-eight years old, born on the eleventh day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuhui, his grandfather Zhihui, and his father Yingyi; his mother was née Zhu. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Jun, Shu, Yi, Cheng, and E; his younger brothers were Zhen, Yuan, and Shi. He married a woman née He. He placed fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Bijin, courtesy name Yizhi, was registered in a military household in Jishui County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Changes, he ranked sixth in birth order and was thirty-three years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ruxue, his grandfather Tao (an assistant prefect), and his father Li. His mother was née Zeng, and his stepmothers were née Hu and née Liu. His father was deceased, and his mother or stepmother was still living. His younger brothers were Bida, Bishu, Biyuan, and Bifeng. He married a woman née Zhou. He placed eighty-sixth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 106th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Wenrui, courtesy name Tinglin, was registered in a civilian household in Xinhui County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Classic of Poetry, he ranked fourth in birth order and was thirty-two years old, born on the twelfth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhenzong, his grandfather Kuan, and his father Song (a prefectural school instructor); his mother was née Li. His mother alone was still living. His elder brothers were Wenchong (an honorary official recognized for public benefactions), Jun, Cheng, Wenkui, Wenju, Wenxuan, Wenxing, and Wenfu. He married a woman née Kuang. He placed sixty-seventh in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and 157th in the Metropolitan Examination.

馬朝卿〔貫山東濟南府武定州陽信縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字臣夫，行一，年三十八，十一月十五日生〕。曾祖福海，祖昇，父聰，前母李氏，母紀氏，繼母曾氏。慈侍下，弟朝佐，娶張氏，繼娶季氏。山東鄉試第二十六名，會試第一百二十名。

translation_en:
Zhang Wenwang 張文瀇, courtesy name Gongsu, was registered in a civilian household in Shangyu County, Shaoxing Prefecture, Zhejiang, and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Changes; he ranked fifteenth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged forty-one, and was born on the thirtieth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Hui; his grandfather, Yue; and his father, Qi, who received the honorary title of Secretary in the Ministry of Works; his mother, née Huang, was posthumously granted the title Lady of Peace, and his stepmother was née Hu. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother; his elder brothers were Wenyuan 文源 and Wenyuan 文淵, the latter a Secretary in the Ministry of War; his wife was née Cheng. He placed fifty-third in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 129th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Xi 王璽, courtesy name Qingbao, was registered with the Wuxiang Left Guard and was a native of Anfu County, Jiangxi; he was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, ranked fourth among his brothers and male cousins, was aged forty-three, and was born on the twentieth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shuaibin; his grandfather, Qizhi; his father, Zhuoyue; and his mother, née Zhou. Both parents were deceased; his wife was née Liu. He placed twenty-seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ma Chaoqing 馬朝卿, courtesy name Chenfu, was registered in a military household in Yangxin County, Wuding Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, and was a student of the Imperial University specializing in the Book of Odes; he ranked first among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-eight, and was born on the fifteenth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fuhai; his grandfather, Sheng; his father, Cong; his father's former wife, née Li; his mother, née Ji 紀; and his stepmother, née Zeng. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother; his younger brother was Chaozuo; he married a woman née Zhang and subsequently a woman née Ji 季. He placed twenty-sixth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 120th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Luan 劉欒, courtesy name Ruqiao, was registered in a civilian household in Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, and was a native of the Tunliu Battalion in that prefecture; he was a prefectural government student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals, ranked second among his brothers and male cousins, was aged thirty-six, and was born on the eleventh day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Fu 福; his grandfather, Jin; his father, Fu 輔, a Professor in a princely establishment; his father's former wife, née Gan; and his mother, née Jin. Both parents were living; his elder brother was Li and his younger brother Yue; his wife was née Wang. He placed fifth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 210th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Kai, courtesy name Tingjin, was registered in the official household category in Wanquan Left Guard under the Wanquan Regional Military Commission, and was a native of Jizhou, Shandong. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the nineteenth day of the ninth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ju, his grandfather Wang, and his father Zheng, an honorary official for public beneficence; his father's former wife was née Jiang, and his mother was née Xu. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Qin, Yue, and Luan, the last an Imperial University student. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Tong. He placed forty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventy-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Luan, courtesy name Yinghe, was registered in the military household category in Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. A department school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was second in birth order, aged forty, and born on the fourteenth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xing, his grandfather Gang, his father Xiu, and his mother née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Feng and Yan, and his younger brothers Qi, Peng, and Lu. He married a woman née Fu. He placed fifteenth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 196th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yuanzheng, courtesy name Shunqing, was registered in the civilian household category in Zhouzhi County, Xi'an Prefecture, Shaanxi. A county school student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the second day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather Rong was posthumously appointed Prefect; his grandfather Xi was a Prefect and received the honorary title of Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission; his father Fu was Chief Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; and his mother, née Zhao, received the title Lady of Respect. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother Yuankai was a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the same examination cohort, and his younger brother Yuanheng was a tribute scholar (gongshi). He married a woman née Yang. He placed second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yi Zan, courtesy name Tingyong, was registered in the civilian household category in Suning County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, and was a native of Linfen County, Shanxi. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was sixth in birth order, aged thirty, and born on the fifth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhitai, his grandfather Shu, a Registrar, his father Ang, and his mother née Bai. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Xun, Zhen, Qi, Jin, and Tian. He married a woman née Wang. He placed 135th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 202nd in the Metropolitan Examination.

任洛〔貫河南開封府鈞州民籍，州學生，治禮記，字仲伊，行十二，年二十七，二月十五日生〕。曾祖克讓，祖諒〔義官〕，父昇〔義官〕，前母程氏，母焦氏。慈侍下，兄顯、濬、熲、顒〔監生〕、顎、江、漢、溥、澳、淇、汴，娶劉氏。河南鄉試第四名，會試第三百四名。

余守觀〔貫湖廣衡州府衡陽縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字尚賓，行三，年三十二，九月初九日生〕。曾祖潭龍，祖洪，父夔，母王氏。具慶下，兄守明，弟守覲、守規，娶歐陽氏。湖廣鄉試第二十四名，會試第九十七名。
translation_en:
Cao Gui 曹珪, courtesy name Tingxian, was registered in a civilian household in Huanggang County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-seven, born on the nineteenth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhen, his grandfather Liangfu, and his father Yi; his mother was née Chao and his stepmother née Shao. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brother was Xiang, and his younger brothers were Bi, Lie 獵 [?], Yao, Sui, Xi, Qi, and Cong. He married a woman née Shu. He placed tenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 296th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gong Jin 龔進, courtesy name Sizhong, was registered in a guardsman's household of the Embroidered-uniform Guard and was a native of Gao'an County, Jiangxi. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the eighth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Lizheng, his grandfather Zhang, and his father Quan; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Xun, and his younger brothers were Dao, Da, and Yu. He married a woman née Ao. He placed fifty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 209th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ren Luo 任洛, courtesy name Zhongyi, was registered in a civilian household in Junzhou, Kaifeng Prefecture, Henan. A student of the subprefectural school specializing in the Book of Rites, he ranked twelfth among his brothers and was aged twenty-seven, born on the fifteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Kerang; his grandfather Liang and father Sheng both held the honorary designation of Official of Righteousness. His father's former wife was née Cheng, and his mother was née Jiao. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Xian, Jun, Jiong, Yong (a student of the Directorate of Education), E, Jiang, Han, Pu, Ao, Qi, and Bian. He married a woman née Liu. He placed fourth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 304th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Shouguan 余守觀, courtesy name Shangbin, was registered in a military household in Hengyang County, Hengzhou Prefecture, Huguang. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he ranked third among his brothers and was aged thirty-two, born on the ninth day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Tanlong, his grandfather Hong, and his father Kui; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Shouming, and his younger brothers were Shoujin and Shougui. He married a woman née Ouyang. He placed twenty-fourth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

陳寀〔貫直隸蘇州府常熟縣民籍，國子生，治詩經，字原大，行二，年三十五，十一月十八日生〕。曾祖繼芳，祖璇，父稷〔贈監察御史〕，母譚氏〔封太孺人〕。慈侍下，兄察〔監察御史〕，娶顧氏，繼娶曹氏。應天府鄉試第三名，會試第九名。

吳棟〔貫義勇後衛籍，順天府東安縣人，縣學生，治詩經，字子材，行一，年三十，十一月二十五日生〕。曾祖榮，祖□，父浩，母杜氏，繼母歐氏。具慶下，弟椿、松、檜、相、楫，娶李氏。順天府鄉試第六十四名，會試第二百七十九名。
translation_en:
Liu Jingyi 劉景沂, courtesy name Tongren, belonged to a military household registered in Changqing County, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong. He was Instructor at the Shangyuan County Confucian School in the directly administered metropolitan region and specialized in the Book of Changes. His family birth order is recorded as 二二四 [?]; he was forty-three, born on the second day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Dazhang, his grandfather Sheng, and his father Rui, formerly an Administrator (changshi); his mother was née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Jingyan, and his wife was née Miao. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shandong Provincial Examination and 212th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Cai 陳寀, courtesy name Yuanda, belonged to a civilian household registered in Changshu County, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, second in family birth order, and thirty-five years old, born on the eighteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jifang, his grandfather Xuan, and his father Ji, posthumously appointed Investigating Censor; his mother, née Tan, was granted the title Grand Lady (ta孺ren). His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brother Cha was an Investigating Censor. He married a woman née Gu and subsequently a woman née Cao. He placed third in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Cai Dan 蔡旦, courtesy name Zhoufu, belonged to a military household registered in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian. He was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes, fifth in family birth order, and thirty-four years old, born on the sixteenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Xuan, his grandfather Zuo, his father He, and his mother née He. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His elder brothers were Ming, Yi 晹, Chen, and Xu 昫; his younger brothers were Bian 昪, Qing 暒, Zhou 晭, and Zhu 曯. His wife was née Shen. He placed fifteenth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 105th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wu Dong 吳棟, courtesy name Zicai, was registered with the Yiyong Rear Guard and was a native of Dong'an County, Shuntian Prefecture. He was a county Confucian school student specializing in the Book of Odes, first in family birth order, and thirty years old, born on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Rong, his grandfather □ [illegible], and his father Hao; his mother was née Du and his stepmother née Ou. His father and stepmother were both living. His younger brothers were Chun, Song, Gui, Xiang, and Ji, and his wife was née Li. He placed sixty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 279th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Ren De, registered in □□□, was an additional student at the Weihui Prefectural School and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhushan; he ranked fourth in his family and was twenty-six years old, born on the fifth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Heng, his grandfather Guang, and his father Hui; his mother was née Yao. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Gang, Zuo, and Yi; his younger brothers were Xiaoxian, Zheng, and Yidao. He married a woman née Huang. He placed sixty-eighth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 128th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Ji was registered with the Tengxiang Right Guard and was a native of Lantian County, Shaanxi. He was a student at the Dingzhou School and specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Ruji; he ranked third in his family and was twenty-five years old, born on the fourth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Dechuan, his grandfather Jie, and his father Sheng, a former prefect [?]; his mother was née Zong. His mother alone was living. His elder brothers were Yue and Shu; his younger brothers were Yuan and Qian. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed thirty-third in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 228th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bian Yin held civilian registration in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, Zhili. He was an additional student at the county school and specialized in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Chaoyan; he ranked first in his family and was twenty-six years old, born on the twelfth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was 𤣱 [reading uncertain], his grandfather Lun, and his father Yuxiao; his mother was née Cao. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Qian, Mi, Zhi, and Xie. He married a woman née Zhao. He placed sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 159th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yang Chaofeng held civilian registration in Anhua County, Qingyang Prefecture, Shaanxi. He was a student at the prefectural school and specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yingshi; he ranked fourth in his family and was twenty-five years old, born on the fourteenth day of the fourth month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, posthumously granted the title □□; his grandfather’s name was □□□. His father was Lun, Right Vice Censor-in-chief of the Censorate; his mother was née Wang, granted the title of Lady (ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tian□, Yifeng (a tribute scholar), Mingfeng, Yunfeng, Chufeng, and Caifeng; his younger brother was Yufeng. He married a woman née Gao. He placed second in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and ninety-third in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Shi Jin, registered in a military household in Huangmei County, Qizhou, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Nanzhong; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-six, and born on the twenty-second day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jie, his grandfather Qing, his father Di, and his mother née Guan. His grandfather and both parents were living. His younger brothers were Luan, Lian, Ming, and □; his wife was née Hong. He placed sixty-seventh in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 253rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Yanqing, registered in a civilian household in Ji County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhongcheng; he was second in birth order, aged thirty-two, and born on the thirtieth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Duo; his grandfather Jie was an Investigating Censor; his father Ji was an Assistant Surveillance Commissioner; and his mother, née Duan, had been granted the title Lady of Suitability. Both parents were living. His elder brother Yanrui was a Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel; his younger brother was Yanzuo. His wife was née Wang. He placed thirty-first in the Henan Provincial Examination; his Metropolitan Examination rank is partly illegible: □□八 [ending in eight].

Gu Zhu, registered in a postal-relay household in Tongchuan Subprefecture, Sichuan, and originally from Wu County in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Mingfu; he was first in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shijie, his grandfather Li, his father Daqin, and his mother née Liu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Ke and Ban; his wife was née Tan. He placed fifty-ninth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 291st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Xu, registered in an official household of Jiuxi Guard, Huguang, and originally from Xi County, Henan, was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zihou; he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-one, and born on the twenty-sixth day of the eighth lunar month. His great-grandfather Yong and grandfather Zhen were both Battalion Commanders; his father Bi was an Associate Prefect; his mother was née Zhang. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Tianjue, Tianmin, and Tiandong, the last an Assistant Commander; his younger brother was Tianzhi. His wife was née Chen. He placed fifty-fifth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 312th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhang Qin 張欽 was registered with Tongzhou Right Guard in Zhili and was a native of Gushi County, Henan. A student of the Tongzhou government school in Shuntian Prefecture, he specialized in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Jingzhi; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-five years old, born on the ninth day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather □ (illegible), and his father Hao; his mother was née Zang. Both parents were living. He married a woman née Su. He placed twenty-first in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 284th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Rao Fu 饒富 was registered as a civilian in Chongren County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Hongji; he ranked third among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the eighteenth day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xuyan 勗妍 [?], his grandfather Bichen, and his father Yuanding; his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shi and An; his younger brothers were Yu, Xian, Cha, and Chong. He married a woman née Huang. He placed twentieth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 309th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhan Shi 詹軾 was registered as a civilian in Yushan County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Jingzhi; he ranked seventeenth among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the twentieth day of the eleventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Shaoxian, his grandfather Bocheng, and his father Zhiwen; his mother was née Li. His father was living and his mother deceased. His elder brothers were Chen, Chong, and Fu; his younger brothers were Xun, Qi, and Jun. He married a woman née Chen. He placed nineteenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and eighty-first in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Chong 劉翀 was registered in a military household in Pinglu County, Pingyang Prefecture, Shanxi. A student of the National University, he specialized in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Wenxiang; he ranked second among his brothers and was thirty-six years old, born on the thirtieth day of the tenth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Sheng, his grandfather Xuan, and his father Liangxin; his mother was née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Han〔a National University student〕; his younger brothers were 𦐥, 𦐣, and 𦐨 [readings uncertain: ?]. He married a woman née Wang. He placed thirty-first in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 153rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Zhang, registered in a civilian household in Taicang Department, Suzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, was a departmental school student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Chaoxiang; he ranked second among his brothers and was twenty-seven years old, born on the tenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Tingbi, his grandfather Shan, his father Yin, and his mother née Lu. His grandfather and both parents were living. His elder brother was Ying; his younger brothers were Lin, Chong, Fan, Jie, and Pu. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Huang. He placed 130th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 250th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Dang Chengzhi, registered in a military household in Xin Department, Taiyuan Prefecture, Shanxi, was a departmental school student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Ruxiao; he ranked first among his brothers and was twenty-six years old, born on the twelfth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather was Xiang, Vice Magistrate of a Department; his grandfather was Yongling, an honorary official; his father was Mao, a District Magistrate; and his mother was née Man. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Chengmei, Cheng’en, Chengci, Chengxian, Chengguang, and Chengxue. He married a woman née Liao. He placed sixtieth in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 323rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhang Shanjing, registered in a civilian household in Shunde County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, was an additional student at the county school, specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Lifu; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was twenty-five years old, born on the ninth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Kangde, his grandfather Huan, a tribute student, his father Shu, and his mother née Liang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shanshu, a government school student, Shan’e, and Shansong; his younger brothers were Shanlun, Shanxue, Shantong, Shanji, and Shande. He married a woman née Li. He placed twenty-eighth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and eighty-second in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zhou Qing, registered in a civilian household in Zhuxi County, Yunyang Prefecture, Huguang, and originally from Wan’an County, Jiangxi, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Runing; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-one years old, born on the twentieth day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Zhenggang; his grandfather’s name is illegible (□), as is his father’s (□□); his mother was née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Zhi; his younger brothers were Jie and Pu. He married a woman née Xi. He placed fifteenth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and ninety-sixth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Jin, registered in an officer household of Zhuolu Central Guard in Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Ruli. He ranked first in birth order, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the fourteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Bin, Vice Commander of a Guard; his grandfather was Gui; and his father was Wenhua, a District Magistrate. His mother was née Bu, and his stepmother née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Qin, Zhen, and Tang, the last a Vice Commander of a Guard; his younger brothers were Qian, Hui, and Jie. He married a woman née Shen. He placed 110th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 179th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Qi Xiong, registered in a civilian household in Jinhua County, Jinhua Prefecture, Zhejiang, was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Shiying. He ranked third in birth order, was aged thirty-four, and was born on the first day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Hu, an Investigating Censor; his grandfather was Tianlin, Right Office Manager of the Office of Transmission; and his father was Ang, an Investigating Censor (the annotation also says “granted the title Lady,” apparently misplaced [?]). His mother was née Xu, granted the title Lady, and his stepmother née Wang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Xi, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Xun; his younger brothers were Hao and Qiong. He married a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-fifth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 261st in the Metropolitan Examination.

□□ Shu, registered in a military household in Wenjiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Wenju. Two characters preceding his age are illegible. His age is given as thirty-four, and his birthday as the twenty-fifth day of the “seventeenth month” [?]. His great-grandfather was Guichun; his grandfather was Siqing; and his father was Li. His mother was née Zheng, and his stepmother née Hao. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Hongqi, a student of the Directorate of Education, and Hongdao, an honorary official; his younger brother was Hongzhan. He married a woman née Ao. He placed twenty-fourth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 169th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Gong Shan, registered in a Confucian scholar household in Xuancheng County, Ningguo Prefecture, Zhili, was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Guozhen. He ranked fourth in birth order; the following age notation, “十四十八,” is garbled [?]. He was born on the seventeenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Youjin, Minister of War; his grandfather’s name is illegible (□); and his father was Boling. His mother was née Xu, and his stepmother née Chen. His father was deceased, and he attended upon his living mother. His elder brother was Ying; his younger brothers were Huan and Xuan. He married a woman née Wei. He placed twenty-sixth in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and seventieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Xian Shangwen 冼尚文 was registered in a civilian household in Panyu County, Guangzhou Prefecture, Guangdong, and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Zhifu; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty-one, born on the twenty-eighth day of the twelfth month. His great-grandfather was Zhong; his grandfather was Cheng [illegible annotation]; his father was Lu [illegible annotation]; and his mother was née Zeng. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Shangyi, Shangli, Shangzhi, and Shangda. He married a woman née Lao and subsequently a woman née Zhang. He placed sixty-fifth in the Guangdong Provincial Examination and fiftieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Mengxu 李孟旭 was registered in a civilian household in Lingqiu County, Yu Subprefecture, Datong Prefecture, Shanxi, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Daxin; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged thirty-six, born on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather’s and father’s names are illegible. His mother was née Zhao, and his stepmothers were née Sun and née Liu. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Menghui [illegible annotation], and his younger brother was Meng’ang [illegible annotation]. He married a woman née Wang. He placed forty-third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and 190th in the Metropolitan Examination.

□□ Qu □□驅 [the first two characters of the name are illegible] was registered in a military household in Kai Subprefecture, Daming Prefecture, Zhili, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Yongzhuan; he ranked second among his brothers and was aged twenty-nine, born on the third day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather was Ying; his father’s name is illegible; and his mother was née Guo. His father was deceased, and his mother was living. His elder brother was Su, and his younger brother was Gua. He married a woman née Shi. He placed 114th in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Ouyang Kun 歐陽崑 was registered in a civilian household in Taihe County, Ji’an Prefecture, Jiangxi, and was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name and his order among his brothers are illegible. He was aged thirty-two, born on the third day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Tang, a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice; his grandfather was Chuang [illegible annotation]; his father was Tingchen; and his mother was née Xiao. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His elder brothers were Xiang, Song (a metropolitan graduate of the bingxu year,  ﬁ1506), and Gui. He married a woman née Guo. He placed seventeenth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 183rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yan Zhu, registered in Neijiang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a guard-officer household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Tingguang, and he ranked second among his brothers. He was thirty-eight, born on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Benxuan, his grandfather Zhengxiang, and his father Erchang; his mother was née Yang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Jin’ao, and his younger brothers were Jinba and Jinchi. His wife was née Yuan. He placed □十一 [?] in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 241st in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yuan, registered in Shangrao County, Guangxin Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student. He specialized in the Classic of Changes. His courtesy name was Jingyan, and he ranked twenty-eighth among his brothers. He was forty-one, born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather’s and grandfather’s names are illegible (□□ and □□); his father was Yunxing, his mother née Zhan, and his stepmother née Hu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were Chu, □, Mo, Fang, □, and De [division of names uncertain]. His wife was née Jiang. He placed 356th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 180th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Liu Wenyuan, registered in Peng County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student. He specialized in the Classic of Documents. His courtesy name was Boru, and he ranked second among his brothers. The following four characters, apparently recording his age, are illegible (□□□□). He was born on the fifth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Jiucheng, his grandfather’s name is illegible (□□), and his father was Lun; his mother was née Li. His father was deceased, and he attended his surviving mother. His wife was née Zhu. He placed 第七□□ [?] in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 第二百六□ [?] in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Qiong, registered in Fuliang County, Raozhou Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and was an added student of the county school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry. His courtesy name was Xian□□ [?]; his birth order and age are illegible (□□ and □□). He was born on the tenth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Xi, and his father Lun. His father’s former wives were née Zheng and née Li; his mother was née Xu, and his stepmother née Chen. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yu, Shan, and Jing, and his younger brother was Qi. His wife was née Li. He placed 69th in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 151st in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Yu Ao, registered in Dingyuan County, Fengyang Prefecture, in the directly administered region, belonged to an artisan household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Dazhen. First in birth order, he was thirty-six years old and was born on the second day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Daotong, his grandfather Min, his father □, and his mother née Zhang. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Han and □; his wife was née Chen. He placed seventh in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 104th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Meng Tingke, registered in Wuchang County, Wuchang Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to a military household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was Peizhi. Third in birth order, he was thirty years old and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Yuan, his grandfather Yingzu, his father Yun, and his mother née Ma. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Tinghuai and Tingbing; his younger brothers were Tingmei, Tingmo, and Tingji. His wife was née Zhou. He placed thirtieth in the Huguang Provincial Examination, followed by two illegible characters, □□ [?], and 178th in the Metropolitan Examination.

□□yuan, whose surname and the first character of his given name are illegible [?], was registered in Jinjiang County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian. He belonged to a civilian household and was a student of the Directorate of Education. He specialized in the Book of Changes; his courtesy name was Zhijie. First in birth order, he was thirty-one years old and was born on the twenty-eighth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Yi, his grandfather Kuan (an honorary official recognized for longevity), his father Gang, and his mother née Lin. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Zongqing, Zongjun, Zongcheng, Zonghuai, Zonghe, and Zonghan; his wife was née Cai. He placed forty-fifth in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 113th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Zhen, registered in Jinxian County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, belonged to a civilian household and served as an Assistant Instructor at the prefectural school of Yangzhou in the directly administered region. He specialized in the Book of Odes; his courtesy name was □□. Eighth in birth order, he was forty-two years old and was born on the twenty-seventh day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Mengbin (posthumously granted the title of Registry Manager), his grandfather Tingyong, his father Shizhi, and his mother née Shu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brother was Jian (an Assistant Instructor), and his younger brother was 𨦣 [reading uncertain]. His wife was née Che; he subsequently married a woman née Xu. He placed eleventh in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 143rd in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Guo Wuchang, courtesy name Dajing, was registered in Xiping County, Runing Prefecture, Henan, in a civilian household. A county school student specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fifth in birth order, aged thirty-five, and born on the twentieth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Zizhong; his grandfather, Lin, was a Vice Commander of a Ward; and his father, □, was a Commander of a Ward. His father's former wife, née Wang, was posthumously granted the title Lady (Ruren); his mother, née Liu, was granted the same title. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were □, Lu, Yao, and □; his younger brothers were Liuyi, an Imperial University student, Qishu, and Bahong. He married a woman née Mao. He ranked eleventh in the Henan Provincial Examination and 330th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiao Huai, courtesy name Dongzhi, was registered in the Guilin Central Guard, Guangxi, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Documents, he was first in birth order, aged twenty-seven, and born on the fourteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Luo; his grandfather, Ying; his father, Jing; and his mother, née Liu. His parents and grandparents were living. His younger brothers were Yi, Han, and Si. He married a woman née Jiang. He ranked forty-second in the Guangxi Provincial Examination and sixty-seventh in the Metropolitan Examination.

Lu Shitong, courtesy name Xingzhi, was registered in Fengcheng County, Nanchang Prefecture, Jiangxi, in a military household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twelfth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Jiguang; his grandfather, Beizai; his father, Dechong; and his mother, née Pan. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Shiyang and Shiyong, and his younger brother was Shiyu. He married a woman née Wang and subsequently a woman née Jiang. He ranked fifty-fifth in the Jiangxi Provincial Examination and 145th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Hou Wei, courtesy name □□, was registered in the Pingxi Guard, Huguang, in an official household. An Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged forty-three, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the tenth month. His great-grandfather, Fu, and grandfather, Zheng, were Battalion Commanders; his father, □, was a Commander. His father's former wife was née □, and his mother was née Xia. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Jue, a Commander, and Lu, an Imperial University student; his younger brother was Xun. He married a woman née Xu and subsequently a woman née Li. He ranked forty-second in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 170th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Zhao Degang, registered in Min County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Chongjie; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged twenty-eight, born on the fourteenth day of the fifth month. His great-grandfather was Yun, a county school instructor; his grandfather was Zhun; his father was Chongqi; and his mother was née Lin. His parents and at least one grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Deyu, Defu, and Deyan, and his wife was née Lin. He placed third in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 135th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xie Yuan, registered in Huai’an County, Fuzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to an official household and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Rites. His courtesy name was Shijie; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was aged thirty-three, born on the twenty-seventh day of the third month. His great-grandfather was De’an; his grandfather was Zhao, granted the title of supervising secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for Military Affairs; and his father was Cong, a county magistrate. His legal mother was née Chen, and his birth mother was née Shang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Hong and Chun, and his younger brothers were Han and Jing. His wife was née Chen. He placed sixty-second in the Fujian Provincial Examination and sixty-ninth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang Yong, registered in Huarong County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, belonged to an artisan household and was an additional student of the county school specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Zixian; he ranked first among his brothers and was aged thirty, born on the twenty-third day of the ninth month. His great-grandfather was Wencheng; his grandfather was Sijin; his father was Jun’ang; and his mother was née Fu. Both parents were living. His younger brothers were Tingchen, Tingbiao, Tingyi, Tingzhi, Tingzhao, Tinggao, and Tingce, and his wife was née Shen. He placed eighth in the Huguang Provincial Examination and 318th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Chen Lie, registered in Zhangpu County, Zhangzhou Prefecture, Fujian, belonged to a civilian household and was a county school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Chaochen; he ranked sixth among his brothers and was apparently aged thirty-eight [?; the age text is garbled], born on the sixteenth day of the eleventh month. His great-grandfather was Zeyi, posthumously granted the title of bureau director in the Ministry of Personnel; his grandfather was Xun; and his father was Heng. His mother was née Yang, and his stepmother was née Zheng. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brother was Xun, his younger brother was Shu, and his wife was née Dai. He placed forty-seventh in the Fujian Provincial Examination and 308th in the Metropolitan Examination.

段理〔貫陝西平凉府鎮原縣，民籍，國子生，治易經，字伯溫，行一，年三十八，七月二十二日生〕。曾祖達〔訓導〕，祖翔，父銓，母朱氏。重慶下，弟琳、瓘、璋、珏、琨、瓛、瓚，娶張氏。陝西鄉試第四十五名，會試第三百七名。

邊憲〔貫直隸河間府任丘縣，官籍，國子生，治書經，字克明，行四，年三十八，四月二十六日生〕。曾祖復初〔贈都察院左副都御史〕，祖永〔戶部郎中，贈都察院左副都御史〕，父鏞〔南京刑部右侍郎〕，前母王氏〔贈淑人〕，母徐氏〔封淑人〕。慈侍下，兄宗〔監生〕、寅〔義官〕、寵〔都察院右副都御史〕，弟寍〔貢士〕、宓〔監生〕、守，娶鄭氏。順天府鄉試第四十四名，會試第一百六十五名。
translation_en:
Gong Dayou, registered in Wujin County, Changzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), belonged to a military household and was a prefectural school student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shiqian; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-eight sui, born on the seventh day of the third lunar month. His great-grandfather was Lihong, his grandfather Ying, and his father Shen, a Magistrate; his mother was née Yin. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Dashun, Dabang, Dayong, Dalun, Dazhen, and Daren. His wife was née Zhang. He placed eighty-first in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 246th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Li Jie, registered in Yongjia County, Wenzhou Prefecture, Zhejiang, belonged to a salt-producing household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Odes. His courtesy name was Shengzhi; he ranked fifth among his brothers and was forty-three sui, born on the fifth day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Ming, his grandfather Wang, and his father Jun; his father's former wife was née Zhang, and his mother was née Lin. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zeng, Hao, Yu, and Feng, and his younger brother was Xun. His wife was née Shao; he subsequently married a woman née Chen. He placed seventy-ninth in the Zhejiang Provincial Examination and 134th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Duan Li, registered in Zhenyuan County, Pingliang Prefecture, Shaanxi, belonged to a commoner household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Changes. His courtesy name was Bowen; he ranked first among his brothers and was thirty-eight sui, born on the twenty-second day of the seventh lunar month. His great-grandfather was Da, an Assistant Instructor; his grandfather was Xiang, his father Quan, and his mother née Zhu. His parents and a grandparent were living. His younger brothers were Lin, Guan, Zhang, Jue, Kun, Huan, and Zan. His wife was née Zhang. He placed forty-fifth in the Shaanxi Provincial Examination and 307th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Bian Xian, registered in Renqiu County, Hejian Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), belonged to an official household and was a National University student specializing in the Book of Documents. His courtesy name was Keming; he ranked fourth among his brothers and was thirty-eight sui, born on the twenty-sixth day of the fourth lunar month. His great-grandfather Fuchu was posthumously granted the title of Left Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His grandfather Yong was a Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, posthumously granted the title of Left Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His father Yong (鏞) was Right Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing. His father's former wife, née Wang, was posthumously granted the title Shuren, Lady of the Third Rank; his mother, née Xu, was granted the same title during her lifetime. His mother was living and his father deceased. His elder brothers were Zong, a National University student; Yin, an honorary official; and Chong, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Censorate. His younger brothers were Ning, a tribute scholar (gongshi); Mi, a National University student; and Shou. His wife was née Zheng. He placed forty-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 165th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wan Qi 萬玘, courtesy name Zongyu, was registered in a military household of Guide Guard and was a native of Guide Subprefecture, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was third in birth order, aged forty-one, and born on the ninth day of the eighth month. His great-grandfather was Cheng; his grandfather, Gui; his father, Hai (a commoner honored for longevity [?]); and his mother, née Wu. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Shan and Xu, and his younger brother was □. His wife was née Meng. He ranked fortieth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 238th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Luo Yu 羅玉, courtesy name Rucheng, was registered in a civilian household in Nanchong County, Shunqing Prefecture, Sichuan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was first in birth order, aged thirty-three, and born on the twenty-eighth day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Zhi; his grandfather, Qing (an honorary official for public benefactions); his father, Zi (also an honorary official for public benefactions); and his mother, née Yang. Both parents were deceased. His younger brothers were Wang 王 [?], Wan, Yao, Jie, Xi, and Huan. His wife was née Yang. He ranked thirty-fifth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 247th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shen □ 沈□, whose courtesy name is illegible (□□), was registered in a military household of □□ Guard and was a native of Cixi County, Zhejiang. A prefectural government student specializing in the Book of Changes, he was second in birth order, aged twenty-nine, and born on the fifth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Qi; his grandfather, Dao (annotation illegible: □□); his father, Kai; and his mother, née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Gao, Zhe, and Yan; his younger brothers were Bian, Heng, Chen, and Quan. His wife was née Sun. He ranked 111th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 274th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Feng Shichang 馮世昌, courtesy name Jisheng, was registered in a military household of Ningshan Guard and was a native of Huojia County, Henan. A student of the Directorate of Education specializing in the Book of Odes, he was fourth in birth order, aged thirty-six, and born on the twenty-third day of the sixth month. His great-grandfather was Li; his grandfather, Zheng; his father, Qin (a county magistrate); and his mother, née Wang. His father was deceased and his mother living. His elder brothers were Shi’an and Shining; his younger brothers were Shikang, Shiqing, and Shirong. His wife was née Xu. He ranked twelfth in the Henan Provincial Examination and 230th in the Metropolitan Examination.

熊永懋〔貫四川成都府資陽縣軍籍，國子生，治詩經，字□□，行二，年三十六，二月初十日生〕。曾祖從真，祖志翰，父赦，母秦氏。具慶下，兄永秀、永仁、永斆，弟永英、永慤、永隆，娶周氏。四川鄉試第四十六名，會試第二百五十六名。
translation_en:
Pan Qi, registered in a civilian household in Wuyuan County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region (Zhili), was a Confucian scholar specializing in the Book of Documents; his courtesy name was Xihe, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-one, born on the tenth day of the seventh month. His great-grandfather was Quancheng; his grandfather was Jiongzi [?], posthumously granted an illegible title; his father was Jin; and his mother was née Hu. Both parents were deceased. His elder brothers were □□ and Jing [?], and his wife was née Hu. He placed 115th in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 226th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Zheng Yunxiang, registered in a military household in Macheng County, Huangzhou Prefecture, Huguang, was a county government school student specializing in the Spring and Autumn Annals; his courtesy name was Shifeng, he ranked third among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-seven, born on the seventh day of the first month. His great-grandfather was Xin, his grandfather Daoming, and his father Ban; his father's principal wife was née Cai, and his birth mother was née Yu. The notation concerning his parents' survival is illegible [?]. His younger brother was Yunxing, and his wife was née Yang. He placed forty-fourth in the Provincial Examination for an illegible jurisdiction and 298th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Wang □□, registered in a civilian household in Qinshui County, Zezhou, Shanxi, was a county government school student specializing in the Book of Rites; his courtesy name was Mingqing, he ranked fourth among his brothers, and he was aged twenty-five, born on the twenty-first day of the first month. His great-grandfather's name is illegible; his grandfather was Tan, posthumously granted the title of Investigating Censor; his father was Ci, a Surveillance Vice Commissioner; and his mother was née Zhang, granted the title of Lady (Ruren). Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Ting, Ru, and Fu, and his younger brothers were Jun, Yi, and Yu; his wife was née Teng. He placed third in the Shanxi Provincial Examination and fortieth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Xiong Yongmao, registered in a military household in Ziyang County, Chengdu Prefecture, Sichuan, was an Imperial University student specializing in the Book of Poetry; his courtesy name is illegible, he ranked second among his brothers, and he was aged thirty-six, born on the tenth day of the second month. His great-grandfather was Congzhen, his grandfather Zhihan, his father She, and his mother née Qin. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were Yongxiu, Yongren, and Yongxue, and his younger brothers were Yongying, Yongque, and Yonglong; his wife was née Zhou. He placed forty-sixth in the Sichuan Provincial Examination and 256th in the Metropolitan Examination.

translation_en:
Wang Ji 王紀, registered in Taizhou, Yangzhou Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military artisan household and was a student of the subprefectural school. He specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name was Liqing. Fifth in birth order, he was aged thirty-six and was born on the eighteenth day of the twelfth lunar month. His great-grandfather was Xiusan, his grandfather Bin, his father Zan, and his mother née Huang. Both parents were living. His elder brothers were □□ and Yi, and his younger brother was Tong; his wife was née Fan. His rank in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination is illegible (□□□); he placed thirty-fourth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Peng Shao 彭韶, registered in Suzhou Guard in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to a military household and was a native of Qingjiang County, Jiangxi. He was a student of the Wu County school and specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name was Zhifu. Second in birth order, he was aged forty-two and was born on the third day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zhonggong, his grandfather □□, his father Chun, and his mother née Liu. His mother alone was living. His elder brother was □□, and his younger brothers were Wei and □; his wife was née Hu. His rank in the Yingtian Prefecture Provincial Examination is illegible (□□□); he placed seventy-eighth in the Metropolitan Examination.

Shi □ 實□ [?], registered in Lulong Guard, Yongping Prefecture, in the directly administered metropolitan region, belonged to an official household and was a student of the Zhuozhou school. He specialized in the Classic of Documents; his courtesy name is illegible (□□). Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-three and was born on the eleventh day of the sixth lunar month. His great-grandfather was □□, his grandfather Tong □, his father □□, and his mother née Liang. Both parents were living. His elder brother was □□ and his younger brother □□; his wife was née Xu. He placed seventh in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 204th in the Metropolitan Examination.

Yu Gui 于桂, registered in Dengzhou, Nanyang Prefecture, Henan, belonged to a civilian household and was a native of Xuancheng County in the directly administered metropolitan region. He was a student of the Directorate of Education and specialized in the Classic of Poetry; his courtesy name is illegible (□□). Second in birth order, he was aged twenty-two and was born on the nineteenth day of the first lunar month. His great-grandfather was Zizhong, his grandfather Qing, his father Xian, and his mother née Li. Both parents were living. His elder brother was Song; his wife was née Liu. He placed seventy-fourth in the Shuntian Prefecture Provincial Examination and 235th in the Metropolitan Examination.
